faq.question: What are the eligibility requirements and prerequisites for the AI Digital Marketing Strategist program?
faq.answer: The program requires basic computer literacy, internet navigation skills, and familiarity with spreadsheets (Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel). No prior programming experience, marketing degree, or commercial advertising background is required. The curriculum begins with business fundamentals before progressing into advanced paid media, analytics, and automation.

faq.question: How does the beginner-to-advanced learning pathway work over the 6 months?
faq.answer: The 6-month journey is divided into sequential phases: Month 1 focuses on business strategy, unit economics, and consumer psychology; Month 2 advances into semantic SEO, technical site crawls, and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO); Month 3 covers brand systems, organic social operations, and Google Ads; Month 4 tackles Meta Ads, creative testing matrices, and GTM/GA4 analytics; Month 5 masters conversion rate optimization, HubSpot CRM, and n8n automation; and Month 6 is dedicated to media budgeting, agency operations, the comprehensive 90-day capstone project, and individual viva voce defense.

faq.question: What is the total duration and guided training hour commitment?
faq.answer: The program comprises exactly 240 guided instructional and laboratory training hours delivered over 6 calendar months across 11 structured modules (53 detailed lessons). In addition to guided class and lab time, students should expect to commit 6–8 hours per week to independent laboratory builds, tool configuration, and portfolio artifact development.

faq.question: What software tools and platforms will I learn hands-on?
faq.answer: You will master 15 core production platforms: Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Tag Manager (GTM), Google Search Console, Looker Studio, Semrush, Screaming Frog SEO Spider, HubSpot CRM, n8n, Brevo, WordPress, ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Canva. Supporting exposure includes Ahrefs, Microsoft Clarity, Meta Business Suite, Claude, Notion, and Adobe Firefly.

faq.question: How are modern AI tools integrated into the curriculum?
faq.answer: Artificial intelligence is taught as an operational accelerator with strict human-in-the-loop governance across all modules. You will learn enterprise prompt engineering (Role, Task, Context, Constraints), customer review mining, multi-angle copywriting, generative visual ideation, and conversational search evaluation (GEO for AI Overviews). We strictly emphasize fact-checking, hallucination mitigation, and copyright compliance, without promoting unverified autonomous spam.

faq.question: What is Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and how is it taught?
faq.answer: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) focuses on understanding how modern conversational answer engines—such as Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Gemini—synthesize search results. You will learn entity mapping, structured data markup, and information gain principles to measure and improve brand citation presence. We teach realistic measurement methodologies without making unscientific promises of guaranteed AI citations.

faq.question: Do I need to spend my own money on paid advertising campaigns?
faq.answer: No. Nova Skills enforces a strict Zero-Student-Ad-Spend Policy. All advertising practicals in Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager are conducted in professional expert draft modes, sandbox accounts, and offline campaign builders (such as Google Ads Editor). You will build complete production-ready campaigns, targeting hierarchies, and creative matrices without risking personal financial capital.

faq.question: How are analytics, GTM conversion tracking, and attribution handled?
faq.answer: You will work with authorized sandbox websites, Google Tag Manager containers, and live Google Analytics 4 demo properties (such as the Google Merchandise Store). You will deploy custom event tags, verify triggers in Tag Assistant Preview mode, designate commercial Key Events, configure exploration funnels, and build interactive multi-channel Looker Studio dashboards calculating blended CPA and ROAS.

faq.question: What will I learn about CRM, lifecycle marketing, and marketing automation?
faq.answer: You will configure real CRM pipelines in HubSpot CRM, design 100-point behavioral lead scoring models, build automated email nurture sequences in Brevo, and construct no-code automation workflows in n8n connecting website form webhooks to CRM contact creation and notifications, complete with error-handling logic.

faq.question: What portfolio projects and capstone deliverable will I complete?
faq.answer: You will build 7 modular portfolio projects (SEO/GEO audit, brand content strategy, Google Ads plan, Meta Ads testing matrix, GTM/Looker Studio dashboard, CRM automation engine, and landing page CRO audit) plus a comprehensive 14-deliverable final capstone: a complete 90-Day Integrated Business Growth Strategy. You will also complete a timed technical troubleshooting laboratory exam and defend your work in an oral viva voce defense.

faq.question: Are the projects based on live or simulated client businesses?
faq.answer: Projects utilize a combination of live sandbox deployments (live WordPress landing pages, active GTM containers, real Looker Studio dashboards) and realistic simulated business scenarios based on real-world agency briefs. All student case studies are clearly documented with verified data inputs, ensuring total transparency and academic integrity.

faq.question: Do I need to pay for software subscriptions during the course?
faq.answer: No. All required hands-on practicals are designed to operate entirely within free software tiers, educational licenses, sandbox accounts, and authorized demo data streams (such as Google Merchandise Store GA4, Screaming Frog free mode, HubSpot free portal, and n8n community/cloud trials).

faq.question: What is the tuition fee and are there EMI options?
faq.answer: The tuition fee for the complete 6-month AI Digital Marketing Strategist program is ₹44,900 INR (applicable taxes/GST extra). Flexible monthly installment (EMI) options are available through approved academic banking partners subject to standard verification.

faq.question: What career transition and placement support is provided?
faq.answer: Nova Skills provides structured career coaching, resume optimization, LinkedIn profile reviews, mock technical interviews, and portfolio defense preparation. While we provide comprehensive portfolio verification that enables graduates to showcase rigorous proof-of-work to prospective employers and agency clients, we strictly refrain from making unrealistic guaranteed job or salary promises.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for complete beginners with no prior marketing experience?
faq.answer: Yes. AI Digital Marketing Specialist is designed specifically for beginners, college students, career switchers, and junior marketing executives. There are no prerequisites other than basic computer and internet literacy. All marketing fundamentals, advertising platforms, and technical concepts are taught step-by-step from scratch.

faq.question: What is the course duration and weekly schedule?
faq.answer: The course runs for 3 Months (12 teaching weeks), delivering exactly 120 guided hours of instructor-led training, live platform walkthroughs, and supervised practical labs (targeting 10 guided hours per week).

faq.question: How much independent practice is expected outside guided training?
faq.answer: We recommend 40 to 60 additional hours of independent practice over the 12 weeks (approximately 3 to 5 hours per week). This time is dedicated to self-paced tool navigation, creative variations, portfolio documentation, and project refinement.

faq.question: Which software tools and platforms will I learn to practical proficiency?
faq.answer: You will develop practical proficiency in core platforms: Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Search Console, Canva, ChatGPT, and Google Gemini. You also gain working proficiency in supporting tools including Google Keyword Planner, Google Trends, Google Business Profile, WordPress, Google Tag Manager, Looker Studio, Meta Business Suite, and Brevo, plus introductory exposure to Semrush, Microsoft Clarity, and Adobe Firefly.

faq.question: What practical projects will I build for my professional portfolio?
faq.answer: You will build 5 tangible portfolio projects: (1) an SEO Audit & Keyword Research Project, (2) a Social Media Content Campaign, (3) a Google & Meta Advertising Setup, (4) a Conversion Landing Page & Tracking Exercise, and (5) an Integrated Local Business Digital Marketing Capstone. These assets form an employer-ready portfolio demonstrating verified proof-of-work.

faq.question: How is AI integrated into the digital marketing curriculum?
faq.answer: AI is integrated as a practical productivity copilot across all modules. You learn structured prompt engineering in ChatGPT and Gemini for buyer persona research, copywriting variations (AIDA/PAS), search intent clustering, and email drafting. You also learn human verification protocols and ethical guidelines to ensure high-quality, commercially compliant marketing output.

faq.question: Do I need to spend my own money on ad budgets or paid software subscriptions?
faq.answer: No. Nova Skills strictly enforces a Zero-Student-Ad-Spend Policy. All paid advertising campaigns across Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager are built in authorized draft modes, sandbox accounts, or offline simulation workbooks. No personal credit cards or ad spending are required. Furthermore, all software used in student labs utilizes free tiers or educational sandboxes.

faq.question: What tools use demonstration properties or authorized simulations?
faq.answer: Google's public GA4 demo account is used for report exploration and traffic analysis, while editable event tagging and Google Tag Manager exercises are conducted on student WordPress sandbox sites. Advanced enterprise SEO tools (Semrush/Ahrefs) are demonstrated via instructor walkthroughs and free exploratory features, ensuring you understand their commercial value without paying $130+/month subscriptions.

faq.question: How are students evaluated for certification?
faq.answer: Certification is evaluated based on practical project deliverables (50%), the integrated capstone portfolio (20%), a timed technical troubleshooting examination (15%), and an oral viva voce defense (15%). Completing these requirements with passing grades awards the Certified AI Digital Marketing Specialist credential.

faq.question: What placement support is provided after graduation?
faq.answer: Students receive dedicated placement assistance, including portfolio reviews, resume optimization for entry-level digital marketing roles, LinkedIn profile enhancement, and interview preparation drills. While we provide active placement support and connect graduates with hiring opportunities, Nova Skills does not make false promises of guaranteed jobs or immediate freelancing wealth.

faq.question: What job roles can I apply for after completing this program?
faq.answer: Graduates are prepared for entry-level digital marketing roles such as Digital Marketing Executive, Junior SEO Executive, Social Media Marketing Executive, Junior Paid Ads Executive, and Digital Marketing Assistant. The curriculum focuses on foundational execution rather than senior management or full-funnel corporate strategy.

modules.module_title: SEO, Local SEO & AI Search Fundamentals
modules.module_purpose: Impart durable, search-engine-compliant organic optimization skills across on-page, local, and basic technical SEO, alongside an evidence-based introduction to AI Overviews and Search Generative Experience (AEO/GEO).
what_you_will_learn: Understand search engine crawling, rendering, indexing, and ranking algorithms.
Conduct keyword research, search intent clustering, and site-wide keyword mapping.
Execute on-page optimization: title tags, meta descriptions, headings, and internal linking.
Diagnose website health using Google Search Console and inspect Core Web Vitals.
Optimize Google Business Profile and local search visibility using NAP consistency and local schema.
Apply evidence-based optimization for AI Overviews and conversational search without unscientific ranking gimmicks.

lessons.what_is_taught: How search engines discover, crawl, render, index, and rank web pages, including robots directives and sitemaps.
subtopics: Search engine architecture: Discovery, crawling, rendering, indexing, and ranking pipelines
Robots exclusion protocol (`robots.txt`) and XML sitemaps (`sitemap.xml`)
Understanding search intent taxonomy: Navigational, Informational, Commercial, Transactional
SERP feature analysis: Organic snippets, Featured Snippets, Knowledge Panels, and People Also Ask
lessons.why_it_matters: Content cannot rank if search engine bots are blocked or unable to render and index pages properly.
lessons.what_learner_does: Inspect and validate a website's `robots.txt` and XML sitemap, identifying crawl barriers and indexing directives.
lessons.expected_outcome: Technical Crawlability & Indexing Diagnostic Sheet.

lessons.what_is_taught: Systematic keyword discovery, search volume estimation, competition analysis, and clustering queries by user intent.
subtopics: Keyword research methodology: Volume, Keyword Difficulty (KD), intent alignment, and business value
Head terms vs. long-tail keywords: Conversion rate dynamics and intent specificity
Keyword clustering workflows using Google Keyword Planner, Google Suggest, and Gemini
Constructing a hierarchical site Keyword Map (URL-to-Keyword intent assignment)
lessons.why_it_matters: Prevents keyword cannibalization and ensures every target page on a website answers a distinct commercial or informational user query.
lessons.what_learner_does: Perform keyword research for a local service website, clustering 15+ keywords across 5 distinct target URLs with primary and secondary search terms.
lessons.expected_outcome: Multi-Page Keyword Map Spreadsheet with Intent Classification.

lessons.lesson_title: On-Page SEO, Content Optimization & Internal Linking
lessons.what_is_taught: Practical on-page content optimization, metadata copywriting, semantic heading hierarchy, and internal linking structures.
subtopics: Title tag architecture, meta description copywriting, and URL slug optimization rules
Semantic heading hierarchy (`H1`, `H2`, `H3`) and structural content organization
Topical depth, keyword density myths, and natural semantic keyword placement
Image SEO: Descriptive filenames, alt text accessibility, and modern WebP compression
Internal linking architecture: Hub-and-spoke models, contextual anchors, and link equity flow
lessons.why_it_matters: Proper on-page formatting and internal linking directly communicate page relevance and topical authority to search ranking algorithms.
lessons.what_learner_does: Draft and optimize title tags, meta descriptions, heading structures, image alt text, and internal link anchors across 5 web pages.
lessons.expected_outcome: Five-Page On-Page SEO Optimization Blueprint.

lessons.what_is_taught: Configuring, verifying, and navigating Google Search Console, diagnosing indexing errors, and understanding Core Web Vitals.
subtopics: Google Search Console setup and verification methods (DNS, HTML tag, GA4 link)
Analyzing the GSC Performance Report: Queries, Pages, Impressions, Clicks, CTR, Average Position
Diagnosing crawl issues via the Page Indexing report and URL Inspection Tool
Core Web Vitals introduction: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
lessons.why_it_matters: Search Console is Google's authoritative direct communication channel for technical indexing health, manual actions, and actual search impressions.
lessons.what_learner_does: Inspect live/diagnostic Search Console performance data, identify non-indexed URLs, run URL Inspection tests, and review Core Web Vitals status.
lessons.expected_outcome: Search Console Technical Audit & Performance Interpretation Report.

lessons.lesson_title: Local SEO, Google Business Profile & Evidence-Based AI Search
lessons.what_is_taught: Local search ranking factors, Google Business Profile optimization, NAP citation consistency, and evidence-based AI search visibility.
subtopics: Google Business Profile (GBP) configuration: Categories, business attributes, services, photos, and reviews
Local 3-Pack ranking signals: Relevance, Distance, and Prominence
NAP (Name, Address, Phone) citation consistency and local directory syndication
Local business structured data: `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD schema generation
Evidence-based Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)
How Google AI Overviews and Gemini-powered search extract citations: factual authority, clarity, and structured entities
Scientific debunking of 'guaranteed AI ranking shortcuts' and fraudulent SEO claims
lessons.why_it_matters: Local businesses rely on local pack visibility and authentic citations for physical foot-traffic and inbound telephone enquiries.
lessons.what_learner_does: Conduct a local SEO audit for a local business, optimize GBP details, generate LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema, and evaluate AI Overview visibility.
lessons.expected_outcome: Local SEO Audit, Google Business Profile Optimization Plan & Schema Markup File.

Building 14-day and 30-day editorial content calendars with clear asset formats and posting cadence
Developing brand voice guidelines, tone adaptability, and visual consistency rules
Community management fundamentals: Response protocols, comment moderation, and customer inquiry routing

lessons.what_learner_does: Build a comprehensive 14-day multi-channel editorial calendar covering 4 content pillars with post captions, format specs, and scheduled publication dates.

lessons.what_is_taught: Proven direct-response copywriting formulas, feed-stopping hook writing, and conversion-focused call-to-action engineering.

Crafting high-engagement hooks for social feeds and video scripts (the 3-second attention rule)
Headline formulas, curiosity gaps, and benefit-driven copywriting
Call to Action (CTA) hierarchy: Engagement CTAs vs. Conversion CTAs (driving comments, saves, bio clicks, DMs)

lessons.what_learner_does: Write 6 sets of multi-angle social copy using AIDA and PAS frameworks, testing 3 distinct headline hooks and CTAs for each.
lessons.expected_outcome: Multi-Angle Social Copywriting Deck with Tested Hooks & CTAs.

lessons.lesson_title: Visual Design Systems & Canva Ad Creatives
lessons.what_is_taught: Visual hierarchy, typography pairing, color contrast, brand kit setup, and commercial creative production using Canva.

lessons.expected_outcome: Suite of 8 Production-Ready Canva Creatives & Brand Styleboard.

Commercial compliance, copyright safety, and quality control in generative AI assets

modules.module_purpose: Master the mechanics, architectures, bidding strategies, policy constraints, and execution of paid search (Google Ads) and paid social (Meta Ads) advertising without risking personal student capital.
what_you_will_learn: Understand paid advertising auction economics, Ad Rank, Quality Score, and commercial KPI calculations.
Build Google Search campaign architectures with proper ad groups, keyword match types, and negative lists.
Write high-relevance Responsive Search Ads (RSAs) and configure ad assets (sitelinks, callouts).
Analyze search term reports and grasp introductory Performance Max (PMax) and AI Max for Search.
Structure Meta Ads Manager campaigns using ODAX objectives, ad sets, placements, and audience targeting.
Create native Meta instant lead generation forms and apply platform advertising compliance policies.

lessons.lesson_title: Paid Advertising Ecosystem, Auction Economics & Account Governance
lessons.what_is_taught: The paid media landscape, search intent vs. interruption social advertising, auction bidding mechanics, and account governance.
subtopics: Paid advertising ecosystem: Pull marketing (Google Search intent) vs. Push marketing (Meta feed discovery)
Auction models and Ad Rank mechanics: Max CPC bid x Quality Score + Expected Impact of Assets
Deconstructing Quality Score: Expected CTR, Ad Relevance, and Landing Page Experience
Core economic KPI calculations: CPM, CPC, CTR, Conversion Rate, CPL, CPA, and ROAS
Account governance: Google Ads MCC vs. Individual Accounts; Meta Business Portfolio / Manager vs. Personal Ad Accounts
lessons.why_it_matters: Understanding auction math prevents marketers from overbidding on low-intent terms or delivering poor ad experiences that inflate acquisition costs.
lessons.what_learner_does: Calculate Ad Rank, CPC, and ROAS across 3 simulated bidding auction scenarios and map business manager user permissions.
lessons.expected_outcome: Paid Advertising Auction Economics & Account Governance Worksheet.

lessons.lesson_title: Google Search Campaign Architecture, RSAs & Match Types
lessons.what_is_taught: Structuring Google Search campaigns, ad groups, keyword match types, negative keyword hygiene, and responsive search ads.
subtopics: Campaign hierarchy: Account -> Campaign -> Ad Groups -> Keywords & Ads
Keyword Match Types: Broad Match, Phrase Match, and Exact Match mechanics in 2026
Negative Keyword Lists: Account-level, campaign-level, and ad-group-level negative keyword hygiene
Responsive Search Ads (RSA): Formulating 15 diverse headlines, 4 descriptions, and strategic pinning logic
Ad Assets (Extensions): Sitelinks, Callouts, Structured Snippets, Call Assets, and Lead Form assets
Search Term Report analysis: Mining high-converting search queries and pruning budget-wasting terms
lessons.why_it_matters: Properly grouped search campaigns with disciplined negative keyword lists achieve higher Quality Scores and significantly lower cost per click.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build a complete Google Search campaign in draft mode with 2 tightly themed ad groups, match-typed keywords, 1 negative list, 1 full RSA, and 3 ad assets.
lessons.expected_outcome: Google Search Campaign Architecture Blueprint & Draft Ad Group Setup.

lessons.lesson_title: Bidding Fundamentals, Conversion Actions, AI Max & PMax
lessons.what_is_taught: Bidding strategy selection, daily budget pacing, Google conversion actions, and introductory AI Max and Performance Max (PMax).
subtopics: Bidding strategy selection: Manual CPC vs. Smart Bidding (Maximize Clicks, Maximize Conversions, Target CPA, Target ROAS)
Budget controls, daily pacing, delivery methods, and shared budget logic
Google Ads Conversion Actions: Primary vs. Secondary actions and conversion tracking linking
Introduction to Performance Max (PMax): Cross-network inventory, asset groups, audience signals, and required exclusions
Introduction to AI Max for Search: Dynamic headlines/descriptions, final URL expansion, and required brand exclusions
lessons.why_it_matters: Smart bidding algorithms require clean conversion data and strict guardrails to prevent automated systems from exhausting client budget.
lessons.what_learner_does: Configure conversion actions, set bidding targets for a sample ₹30,000 budget, and audit automated search asset settings.
lessons.expected_outcome: Bidding Strategy & Automated Campaign Guardrails Specification.

lessons.lesson_title: Meta Ads Manager Hierarchy, Objectives & Audience Targeting
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating Meta Ads Manager, ODAX campaign objectives, ad set configuration, placement optimization, and audience definitions.
subtopics: Meta Ads Manager hierarchy: Campaign (Objective) -> Ad Set (Audience, Budget, Placement) -> Ad (Creative & Copy)
Campaign Objectives under ODAX: Awareness, Traffic, Engagement, Leads, App Promotion, Sales
Audience targeting taxonomy: Core Audiences (location, demographics, detailed interests), Custom Audiences, Lookalike Audiences
Placement optimization: Advantage+ Placements vs. Manual Placements (Feeds, Stories, Reels)
Budget allocation models: Advantage Campaign Budget (CBO) vs. Ad Set Budget Optimization (ABO)
lessons.why_it_matters: Structuring ad sets and selecting appropriate campaign objectives ensures Meta's machine learning algorithm finds high-converting users efficiently.
lessons.what_learner_does: Set up a Meta campaign in draft mode, configure 2 distinct ad sets targeting local interest clusters and demographic profiles with manual placement testing.
lessons.expected_outcome: Meta Campaign Hierarchy & Audience Targeting Setup Workbook.

lessons.lesson_title: Meta Lead Generation, Instant Forms, Advantage+ & Ad Policy
lessons.what_is_taught: Building native instant lead generation forms, creative formatting, Advantage+ automation features, and platform policy compliance.
subtopics: Building Native Instant Forms: Intro banner, qualifying custom questions, prefill data, privacy policy link, completion screen
Creative formats: Single image ads, multi-card carousels, and vertical video ads
Advantage+ Creative enhancements: Text variations, visual touches, and aspect-ratio adjustments
Retargeting fundamentals: Custom audiences built from web visitors and social page engagement
Platform Advertising Policies: Prohibited content, personal attributes, health/finance claims, and avoiding account suspensions
Zero-spend verification: Testing and reviewing campaign drafts without connecting payment methods
lessons.why_it_matters: Native instant forms capture high-volume mobile leads without landing page load friction; policy compliance prevents devastating account bans.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build a native Meta Instant Form with custom qualifying questions, assemble 2 ad creative variants, and run an ad policy pre-flight check.
lessons.expected_outcome: Native Instant Lead Generation Form Build & Ad Policy Compliance Checklist.

Anatomy of a high-converting landing page: Above-the-fold hero, value proposition, proof elements, benefit matrix, FAQ, footer CTA
Mobile-first responsive UX: Tap targets, sticky CTAs, readable typography, and page speed impacts on bounce rate

Building landing pages with WordPress Block Editor (Gutenberg): Columns, Groups, Covers, Spacers, Buttons
Utilizing lightweight block libraries and responsive visual controls
Configuring responsive breakpoints (desktop, tablet, mobile viewports)

subtopics: Crafting compelling hero headlines and benefit-oriented subheadings that answer 'What's in it for me?'
Call to Action (CTA) hierarchy: Primary vs. Secondary buttons, button microcopy, and color contrast
Trust and credibility architecture: Customer testimonials, review star ratings, partner badges, and security seals
Risk reversal strategies: Guarantees, free trials, transparent pricing, and privacy reassurances

lessons.what_learner_does: Write all landing page copy sections, including hero headline variants, benefit bullet points, testimonial blocks, and button microcopy.
lessons.expected_outcome: Landing Page Conversion Copy Deck with Trust Signal Blueprint.

lessons.lesson_title: Lead Capture Forms, Thank-You Funnels & Lead Magnets

subtopics: Designing high-converting lead capture forms: Field count vs. conversion rate optimization
Installing and configuring WordPress form plugins (WPForms / Fluent Forms)
Building dedicated Thank-You Pages: Setting expectations, next steps, and secondary conversion actions
Lead magnet delivery mechanisms: Direct file download redirects vs. automated confirmation email links

Building tracking URLs using the Google Campaign URL Builder

modules.module_purpose: Provide practical, hands-on mastery over Google Analytics 4 (GA4), web conversion tracking via Google Tag Manager (GTM), data hygiene, and automated executive reporting in Looker Studio.
what_you_will_learn: Navigate GA4 properties, configure web data streams, and analyze Traffic Acquisition reports.
Understand the event-based data model, default events, and mark high-value events as Key Events.
Deploy Google Tag Manager (GTM) containers and configure custom click and form triggers.
Implement and test custom GA4 Event Tags in GTM Tag Assistant Preview mode on sandbox sites.
Calculate core marketing math formulas: CTR, CPC, CPL, CPA, and ROAS.
Build interactive single-page marketing dashboards connecting GA4 and Search Console in Looker Studio.

lessons.lesson_title: GA4 Architecture, Data Streams & Traffic Acquisition Reports
lessons.what_is_taught: The event-based measurement model of GA4, account and property hierarchy, web data streams, Enhanced Measurement, and acquisition reporting.
subtopics: Evolution from Universal Analytics session-based model to GA4 event-driven data model
Account structure: Accounts, GA4 Properties, and Web/App Data Streams
Enhanced Measurement: Automated capture of pageviews, 90% scrolls, outbound clicks, file downloads
Navigating Standard Reports: Acquisition, Engagement, Monetization, and Retention
Traffic Acquisition reporting: Default Channel Groups, Source / Medium, and campaign attribution basics
lessons.why_it_matters: GA4 is the global enterprise standard for web measurement; understanding its data model is essential for accurate marketing attribution.
lessons.what_learner_does: Navigate a GA4 property, inspect data stream settings, analyze traffic acquisition by source/medium, and compare session vs. user metrics.
lessons.expected_outcome: GA4 Traffic Acquisition Analysis & Data Stream Audit Report.

lessons.lesson_title: Google Tag Manager (GTM) Setup, Triggers & Event Tags
lessons.what_is_taught: The purpose of GTM, container architecture, tags, triggers, variables, and deploying custom GA4 event tags.
subtopics: Why use GTM: Decoupling marketing measurement tags from website source code
GTM Hierarchy: Accounts, Containers, Tags, Triggers, and Variables
Built-in Variables (Click URL, Click Classes, Page Path) and custom trigger types (All Clicks, Form Submission)
Deploying the Google Tag on a WordPress website via GTM
Creating custom GA4 Event Tags (e.g., `button_click`, `form_submit`, `generate_lead`)
Using GTM Preview & Debug Mode (Tag Assistant) to inspect tag firing status and trigger conditions
lessons.why_it_matters: GTM empowers marketers to instrument tracking events across websites without writing code or risking site downtime.
lessons.what_learner_does: Install GTM on a sandbox site, configure 3 custom event tags (phone click, CTA button click, form submit), and debug firing in Tag Assistant.
lessons.expected_outcome: Configured GTM Container Export (.json) & Tag Assistant Debug Log.

lessons.lesson_title: Key Events, Conversion Linking & Measurement Hygiene
lessons.what_is_taught: Marking GA4 Key Events (formerly conversions), linking Google Ads and Search Console, and measurement quality standards.
subtopics: The 'Key Events' terminology in GA4: Designating high-value user actions as Key Events
Linking GA4 with Google Ads and Google Search Console accounts
Importing GA4 Key Events into Google Ads for Smart Bidding optimization
Measurement hygiene: Internal traffic filtering (excluding agency/employee IP addresses)
Consent Mode v2 overview and privacy-compliant tracking fundamentals

lessons.why_it_matters: Clean, properly designated conversion data is mandatory for algorithmic ad bidding and reliable client reporting.
lessons.what_learner_does: Mark verified form submission events as Key Events in GA4, review account link settings, and configure internal IP filters.
lessons.expected_outcome: GA4 Key Event Configuration & Measurement Hygiene Plan.

lessons.lesson_title: Core Marketing Math, Commercial Metrics & ROAS Calculations
lessons.what_is_taught: Computational formulas, financial meaning, and diagnostic benchmarks for core commercial marketing metrics.
subtopics: CTR (Click-Through Rate) calculation: (Clicks / Impressions) x 100
CPC (Cost Per Click): Total Ad Spend / Total Clicks
CPL (Cost Per Lead) & CPA (Cost Per Acquisition): Total Cost / Total Conversions
ROAS (Return on Ad Spend): (Total Revenue Generated from Ads / Total Ad Spend) x 100%
Break-Even ROAS, Profit Margin analysis, and Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) vs. Lifetime Value (LTV)
lessons.why_it_matters: Marketing executives are judged on business revenue and acquisition profitability, not vanity engagement impressions.
lessons.what_learner_does: Solve a multi-channel performance calculation problem set, computing CTR, CPC, CPL, CPA, and ROAS across 3 sample client scenarios.
lessons.expected_outcome: Marketing Performance Mathematics & ROAS Calculation Workbook.

lessons.lesson_title: Looker Studio Dashboard Construction & Executive Reporting
lessons.what_is_taught: Connecting Looker Studio to data sources, designing executive dashboards, selecting visual chart types, and writing summary insights.
subtopics: Connecting Looker Studio to GA4 and Google Search Console data connectors
Dashboard layout principles: Scorecards, time-series traffic charts, channel acquisition tables, and device donut charts
Adding interactive date range controls and channel filter dropdowns
Data formatting, conditional formatting heatmaps, and brand styling
Drafting executive summary commentary: Translating data charts into actionable business recommendations
lessons.why_it_matters: Clients and corporate stakeholders expect clear, automated, visual dashboards rather than complex raw analytics tables.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build an interactive, single-page marketing dashboard in Looker Studio connecting live/sample GA4 data, complete with scorecards, charts, and date filters.
lessons.expected_outcome: Live Shareable Looker Studio Marketing Performance Dashboard.

modules.hands_on_practice: Using an authorized test website, implement and validate three important events, then build a simple marketing dashboard.

modules.business_application: Critical competency for digital marketing executives, analytics coordinators, and agency account managers responsible for monthly client reporting.
modules.expected_outcome: Live interactive analytics dashboard and verified web tracking container ready for commercial deployment.

modules.module_purpose: Teach ethical, permission-based email marketing, audience segmentation, conversion-driven copywriting, and automated welcome/nurturing sequences using modern ESP software.
what_you_will_learn: Understand permission-based email marketing, deliverability fundamentals, and compliance laws (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, DPDP).
Manage contact lists, handle unsubscribes, and segment audiences based on engagement and demographics.
Write high-converting email copy, craft compelling subject lines, and design responsive email templates.
Build a 3-part automated welcome and lead nurturing email sequence with delay timers in Brevo.

lessons.what_is_taught: The strategic power of owned audiences, global email compliance regulations, deliverability factors, and spam filter avoidance.
subtopics: Owned marketing channels vs. rented platform algorithms: Long-term asset value
Global email regulations: Consent mechanisms, opt-in rules, physical address requirements, and easy unsubscribes (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, DPDP)
Email deliverability fundamentals: Sender reputation, domain authentication overview (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), and bounce rates
Spam trigger words, sender name consistency, and inbox placement best practices
lessons.why_it_matters: Non-compliant email marketing triggers heavy legal penalties, burned domain reputations, and zero inbox placement.
lessons.what_learner_does: Audit an email newsletter for compliance factors, check domain authentication concepts, and run a spam trigger pre-flight check.
lessons.expected_outcome: Email Compliance & Deliverability Pre-Flight Checklist.

lessons.lesson_title: Audience Segmentation, Contact Lists & Lead Ingestion
lessons.what_is_taught: Contact list management, data hygiene, audience segmentation models, and capturing leads from website forms into an ESP.
subtopics: Contact list hygiene: Opt-in confirmation, handling hard vs. soft bounces, and managing unsubscriptions
Audience segmentation: Demographic, purchase history, website engagement, and open/click recency
Lead capture integration: Routing leads from WordPress form submissions into email lists via native integrations or webhooks
Custom contact attributes: Mapping name, email, phone, location, and interest tags
lessons.why_it_matters: Segmented email campaigns achieve dramatically higher open rates, lower unsubscribe rates, and superior conversion ROI than generic blast emails.
lessons.what_learner_does: Set up a subscriber list in Brevo with custom contact attributes, configure tags, and test lead ingestion from a web form.
lessons.expected_outcome: Brevo Subscriber List Architecture & Ingestion Setup.

lessons.lesson_title: Email Copywriting, Design & Subject Line A/B Testing
lessons.what_is_taught: Anatomy of high-converting emails, direct-response email copywriting, responsive visual template building, and subject line optimization.
subtopics: Anatomy of a marketing email: Sender name, subject line, preheader text, visual hero, body copy, and primary CTA
Email copywriting frameworks: The Soap Opera Sequence, educational storytelling, and urgency/scarcity ethics
Designing responsive, accessible email templates using Brevo's drag-and-drop builder
Subject line psychology, curiosity triggers, preview text pairing, and A/B split testing
lessons.why_it_matters: The subject line determines whether the email is opened; the body copy and CTA determine whether the lead takes commercial action.
lessons.what_learner_does: Draft copy for a 3-part email sequence and design a responsive branded email template inside Brevo.
lessons.expected_outcome: Branded Email Template Design & Multi-Email Copy Deck.

lessons.what_is_taught: Setting up visual marketing automations in Brevo, defining entry triggers, delay timers, and crafting an effective welcome nurturing sequence.
subtopics: Overview of marketing automation workflows: Triggers, delays, conditions, and actions
Setting up the 3-part Lead Nurturing / Welcome Sequence:
• Email 1: Immediate Lead Magnet Delivery & Welcome (sent instantly upon signup)
• Email 2: Brand Story, Problem Agitation & Educational Value (sent Day +2)
• Email 3: Social Proof, Case Study & Direct Call to Action / Offer (sent Day +4)
Testing automated workflows: Submitting test contacts, validating delay timers, and monitoring delivery logs
lessons.why_it_matters: Automated welcome workflows nurture leads immediately while user purchase intent is highest, without requiring manual intervention.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build and activate a live 3-email automated welcome workflow in Brevo, test trigger execution with a sample contact, and verify delivery.
lessons.expected_outcome: Active 3-Part Automated Welcome Sequence in Brevo with Verification Logs.

Deconstructing business goals: Lead generation volume, customer acquisition cost targets, and brand visibility
Multi-channel budget modeling: Allocating a ₹50,000 monthly marketing budget across Search, Social, and Content
Defining unified campaign messaging, value propositions, and cross-channel funnel touchpoints

lessons.what_learner_does: Analyze the selected business case brief, calculate projected channel KPIs, and author an Integrated Campaign Strategy Plan.

lessons.why_it_matters: Real marketing jobs require orchestrating multiple technical platforms into a cohesive, functioning acquisition ecosystem.

lessons.lesson_title: 30-Day Campaign Simulation, Data Analysis & Optimization Plan

A/B test evaluation: Identifying winning ad creative variations and email subject line open rates
Formulating an actionable 30-Day Campaign Optimization Plan based on empirical data findings

lessons.what_learner_does: Analyze a multi-channel performance dataset, identify underperforming ad groups and pages, and write an executive optimization plan.

Compiling high-resolution visual evidence, draft screenshots, GTM container exports, and live dashboard links
Hosting portfolio documentation on professional platforms (Notion, LinkedIn Featured, personal portfolio site, PDF deck)
Resume formatting and interview preparation: Articulating technical competencies for target entry-level marketing roles

why_now.industry_shift: Rising customer acquisition costs and third-party tracking restrictions require modern performance marketers to engineer first-party data layers and master algorithmic media buying.

why_now.career_opportunity: High global demand across performance marketing agencies, fast-growing D2C brands, B2B technology enterprises, and independent media buying retainers.

learning_outcomes: Plan comprehensive performance marketing campaigns aligned with commercial unit economics, customer journey funnels, and business acquisition goals.
Build and optimize high-intent Google Search campaigns in Google Ads Editor using Single-Theme Ad Groups, keyword match types, and negative sculpting.
Configure Google AI Max search capabilities, automatically created assets, and enforce strict negative keyword and brand safety controls.
Plan and structure Performance Max and Google Shopping campaigns with optimized product feeds, segmented asset groups, and layered audience signals.

Diagnose and resolve campaign tracking problems, tag firing errors, duplicate conversion fires, and attribution discrepancies using Tag Assistant and Meta Test Events.

Manage multi-channel advertising budgets, daily pacing models, marginal ROAS thresholds, and forecast customer acquisition costs across business scenarios.
Evaluate campaign experiments and A/B split tests with statistical sample-size calculations, confidence thresholds, and minimum detectable effects.
Recommend data-backed pause, improve, or scale decisions using vertical and horizontal scaling frameworks and marginal efficiency analysis.

stages.desc: Selecting channels, budgets, and targeting.

business_use_cases.business_problem: Low conversion rate and high CPA.
business_use_cases.approach: Implement optimized funnel tracking and targeted ad campaigns.
business_use_cases.output: Increased ROAS and lowered acquisition costs.

ai_integration.ai_can_assist_with: Brainstorming copy, generating data insights, formatting reports.

ai_integration.responsible_use: Maintain data privacy and avoid misleading AI-generated content.

best_practices: Always set up conversion tracking before spending ad budget.
Let data, not assumptions, drive your optimization decisions.
Continuously test new creatives and audiences.

common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Lack of time or understanding of optimization processes.
common_mistakes.professional_approach: Schedule regular performance reviews and iterative testing.

faq.question: Is the Performance Marketing Specialist course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. While prior digital marketing exposure is helpful, it is not mandatory. The course begins with foundational direct response principles, auction economics, and commercial mathematics before progressing to advanced Google and Meta campaign builds. Prerequisites are basic computer literacy, internet navigation skills, and spreadsheet fundamentals (Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel).

faq.question: What is the total duration and guided training hour commitment?
faq.answer: The program spans 4 months and delivers 160 guided instructional hours structured across 9 modular phases, supported by 60–80 hours of recommended independent laboratory practice and capstone project development.

faq.question: What is the tuition fee for the Performance Marketing Specialist program, and does it include GST?
faq.answer: The approved tuition fee is INR 34,900. Goods and Services Tax (GST) of 18% is applicable extra where legally required (totaling INR 41,182). Nova Skills maintains transparent pricing with zero hidden registration charges or unverified comparative discount claims.

faq.question: Are EMI financing options available for this program?
faq.answer: Yes, flexible EMI options are commercially available for eligible applicants, including a 4-month zero-interest installment plan (~INR 10,296/month inclusive of GST) and 6-month flexible financing options through approved education lending partners.

faq.question: Do students need to spend their own personal money on advertising budgets?
faq.answer: No. Nova Skills enforces a strict Zero-Student-Ad-Spend Policy. Students learn campaign architecture, keyword sculpting, and ad configuration using Google Ads Editor offline archives, draft-mode sandbox accounts, GTM Preview Mode, and official Google Merchandise Store demo data. Students are never required or pressured to risk personal funds on live ad auctions.

faq.question: Do I need to purchase expensive third-party software subscriptions?
faq.answer: No. All core professional tools—including Google Ads, Google Ads Editor, Meta Ads Manager, Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Google Merchant Center, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, and Google Sheets—are accessed using free professional tiers, developer sandboxes, or local desktop software.

faq.question: What specific Google Ads training is included in this program?
faq.answer: Students master high-intent Search campaign architecture, Single-Theme Ad Groups (STAGs), keyword match type mechanics (Exact, Phrase, Broad), negative keyword hierarchies, Search Terms Report mining, Responsive Search Ads (RSAs), Quality Score optimization, Ad Rank mechanics, and Smart Bidding algorithms (tCPA, tROAS, Max Conversions).

faq.question: How does the curriculum cover Google AI Max and automated search controls?
faq.answer: Students learn to configure and govern Google AI Max features, Automatically Created Assets (ACA), and generative search themes while maintaining human-in-the-loop oversight through account-level negative keywords, brand exclusions, and 50/50 cookie-split Google Ads Experiments.

faq.question: How are Performance Max (PMax) and Google Merchant Center taught?
faq.answer: Students configure Google Merchant Center product feeds, resolve feed diagnostic errors, apply custom margin labels, structure 3-tier Standard Shopping priority campaigns with query sculpting, and construct multi-channel PMax campaigns with segmented asset groups and custom audience signals.

faq.question: What is covered in the Meta Ads curriculum?
faq.answer: The program covers Meta Business Suite asset governance, ODAX campaign objectives, native Instant Lead Forms, Sales conversion campaigns, Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns (ASC) with existing customer budget caps (10–20%), time-decay retargeting funnels, dynamic catalog ads (DPA), and frequency analysis.

faq.question: How are GA4 event measurement and Google Tag Manager covered?
faq.answer: Students deploy client-side web tracking using Google Tag Manager, configure custom JavaScript dataLayer pushes for lead and e-commerce actions, designate GA4 Key Events, implement Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for web and leads, and verify tag firing in Tag Assistant and GA4 DebugView.

faq.question: What will I learn about Meta Pixel, Conversions API, and event deduplication?
faq.answer: Students deploy Meta Pixel base code and standard events, configure matching unique event_id generators in GTM, transmit server-side CAPI payloads, verify event deduplication in Meta Events Manager, and optimize Event Match Quality (EMQ) scores (target ≥8.0/10) using hashed first-party customer data.

faq.question: What is the scope of Server-Side GTM (sGTM) covered in this course?
faq.answer: Students explore the conceptual architecture of server-side tagging, Cloud Run proxy containers, first-party cookie extension, and Google Consent Mode v2 through guided instructor demonstrations and sandbox walkthroughs, without requiring students to maintain paid personal cloud infrastructure.

faq.question: How are AI tools integrated into the performance media workflow?
faq.answer: Students utilize structured prompt engineering in ChatGPT and Google Gemini to conduct customer review mining, generate 15-headline RSA copy matrices, draft direct-response video scripts, configure automated rules in ad platforms, explore n8n webhook alerts, and enforce human compliance verification against advertising policy violations.

faq.question: Are the practical exercises conducted on live accounts or simulated environments?
faq.answer: The curriculum clearly distinguishes between operational modes: students configure live platform features within free supervised sandbox accounts, offline desktop tools (Google Ads Editor), and GTM preview mode, while utilizing realistic anonymized client datasets for multi-channel budget pacing and Looker Studio dashboarding.

faq.question: What portfolio deliverables and capstone project will I complete?
faq.answer: Students build an 18-deliverable professional portfolio consisting of 7 core projects (Google Search STAG build, GMC/PMax blueprint, Meta Advantage+ build, GTM container JSON, Meta CAPI deduplication log, Landing Page CRO audit, Looker Studio dashboard) and a comprehensive final capstone defended via an oral viva voce examination.

faq.question: What entry-level career pathways does this specialization prepare me for?
faq.answer: Graduates are qualified for specialized acquisition roles including PPC Executive, Paid Media Executive, Junior Performance Marketer, Google Ads Executive, Meta Ads Executive, and Paid Acquisition Associate across digital marketing agencies, D2C retail brands, B2B SaaS companies, and growth consultancies.

faq.question: Does Nova Skills offer placement support or guarantee a job?
faq.answer: Nova Skills provides comprehensive career preparation—including portfolio reviews, technical GitHub/drive repository packaging, resume optimization, and mock technical interviews. In strict accordance with ethical education standards, Nova Skills does not offer guaranteed job placements, salary promises, or artificial hiring quotas.

Offer relevance and Message Match: Synchronizing ad creative hooks with landing page hero headlines, imagery, and promise
Landing-page structure: Above-the-fold value proposition, hero visual, social proof ribbons, problem/solution modules, FAQ accordions, and sticky CTAs
Headlines and CTA hierarchy: Drafting primary value propositions, subheadlines, primary vs. secondary action buttons, and micro-copy

Lead forms: Single-step vs. multi-step lead capture forms, progressive disclosure, social sign-in, and auto-formatting fields

Heatmaps and scroll maps: Analyzing click heatmaps, scroll depth maps, and visual attention maps across desktop and mobile devices
Session recordings: Filtering user sessions by traffic source (Google Ads vs. Meta Ads), device type, and landing page URL
Conversion friction diagnosis: Dead clicks (unlinked elements clicked), rage clicks (rapid frustration clicks), and excessive scrolling
Funnel analysis: Pinpointing the exact page element or field where the majority of prospective leads abandon the conversion path
lessons.why_it_matters: Quantitative metrics show what happened, but behavioral replays in Clarity show why users failed to convert, revealing actionable UX flaws.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyze 15 session recordings and click heatmaps in Microsoft Clarity to identify 3 major UX blockers on a live landing page.

lessons.lesson_title: A/B Testing Methodology, Statistical Basics & Experiment Prioritization
lessons.what_is_taught: Scientific A/B split-testing frameworks, formulating testable conversion hypotheses, sample size limitations, statistical significance basics, and experiment prioritization using PIE / ICE models.
subtopics: Conversion hypotheses: Formulating rigorous test statements: 'If we [change variable X], then [metric Y will improve], because of [behavioral insight Z]'
A/B testing mechanics: Split testing vs. multivariate testing vs. multi-armed bandit approaches
Sample-size limitations: Minimum detectable effect (MDE), baseline conversion rates, required sample sizes, and false positive risks
Statistical interpretation basics: P-values, 95% statistical confidence, statistical power (80%), and avoiding peeking bias
Experiment prioritization: Scoring test ideas using the PIE (Potential, Importance, Ease) and ICE frameworks
UX improvements: Synthesizing winning test variants into permanent production landing page templates
lessons.why_it_matters: Testing without statistical rigor produces false conclusions that damage conversion rates; structured prioritization focuses efforts on highest-impact tests.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build an A/B test plan for an underperforming landing page, calculate sample size requirements for 95% statistical confidence, and prioritize 5 test variants using the PIE model.
lessons.expected_outcome: Complete A/B Test Experiment Design Document & PIE Prioritization Roadmap.

core_projects.project_title: Google Search Ads & AI Max Campaign
core_projects.operational_mode: Offline Build via Google Ads Editor & Supervised Sandbox Draft Mode (Zero Personal Ad Spend Required)
core_projects.business_brief: A high-ticket B2B logistics SaaS platform with an average contract value (ACV) of ₹2,40,000 is launching in a competitive search market. The company needs an intent-driven Google Search account structure, comprehensive negative keyword governance, high-converting Responsive Search Ads (RSAs), and a governed Google AI Max test setup in Google Ads Editor to capture active commercial purchase intent without budget waste.
core_projects.data_requirements: Client discovery brief, seed keyword lists, competitor search visibility reports, historical CPC benchmarks, and landing page URLs.
student_actions: Conduct keyword research to identify 60+ commercial and transactional keywords grouped into 5 Single-Theme Ad Groups (STAGs).
Build account-level, campaign-level, and cross-ad-group negative keyword lists to prevent internal budget cannibalization.
Author a complete Responsive Search Ad (RSA) copy matrix with 15 headlines and 4 descriptions per ad group using direct-response frameworks.
Configure ad assets including Sitelinks with descriptions, Callouts, Structured Snippets, and Lead Form Assets.
Configure Google AI Max automatically created assets (ACA) and establish strict brand exclusion and negative keyword governance.
Build and validate the entire campaign offline in Google Ads Editor, resolving all syntax, URL, and character-limit errors.
exact_deliverables: Validated Google Ads Editor archive (.csv / .aea) ready for import with zero structural errors.
Master Keyword Intent Matrix with match types and negative sculpting lists (.xlsx).
Responsive Search Ad Copy Matrix & Ad Asset Extension Specifications.
Google AI Max Governance & Experimentation Plan.
core_projects.qa_requirements: 100% of keywords mapped to verified search intent; zero character-limit violations (headlines ≤30 chars, descriptions ≤90 chars); all sitelinks have unique destination URLs; negative lists applied at appropriate hierarchy levels.
core_projects.evaluation_rubric: Account hierarchy and STAG structure (30%), negative keyword and match type rigor (25%), RSA copy quality and asset completeness (25%), Smart Bidding and AI Max governance logic (20%).
core_projects.independent_evidence: Validated Google Ads Editor archive file, screenshot of Google Ads Editor error-free validation status, and keyword research workbook.
core_projects.reporting_requirements: Executive 3-page Search Campaign Architecture Brief detailing bidding rationale, keyword strategy, and negative governance.

core_projects.operational_mode: Google Merchant Center Sandbox & Google Ads Draft Mode (Zero Personal Ad Spend Required)
core_projects.business_brief: A multi-category D2C lifestyle apparel brand with a 50-SKU catalog wants to scale e-commerce transactions across Google Shopping and Performance Max. The brand faces frequent feed diagnostic disapprovals, unsegmented PMax asset groups, and overlapping search queries. The client requires a cleansed GMC product feed, a 3-tier Standard Shopping priority structure, and segmented PMax asset groups with layered audience signals.
core_projects.data_requirements: Raw 50-item e-commerce product catalog export with missing GTINs, product images, price/inventory data, and Google taxonomy classifications.
student_actions: Audit and cleanse raw product feed data, engineering titles using [Brand + Product + Attributes + Color + Size] and assigning Google Product Categories.
Configure supplemental feed rules applying Custom Labels (0-4) based on gross profit margin tiers (High/Med/Low) and inventory velocity.
Resolve 5 intentional Google Merchant Center feed diagnostic errors (missing GTINs, shipping mismatches, invalid image URLs).
Design a 3-tier Standard Shopping campaign structure (High, Medium, Low priority) using negative keyword query sculpting.
Construct a Performance Max campaign blueprint with 3 theme-segmented Asset Groups, complete visual/text creative assets, and audience signals.
exact_deliverables: Validated 50-SKU Product Catalog Feed TSV file passing GMC feed validation.
GMC Diagnostic Error Remediation Matrix with before/after status.
3-Tier Standard Shopping Query Sculpting & Negative Keyword Architecture.
Performance Max Master Asset Group Matrix with Customer Match and Custom Intent audience signals.
core_projects.qa_requirements: Zero fatal feed errors in GMC validator; 100% of SKUs contain valid price, availability, and GTIN/MPN; PMax asset groups contain full required image ratios (1:1, 1.91:1, 4:5) and logo assets.
core_projects.evaluation_rubric: Product feed attribute engineering and compliance (30%), PMax asset group relevance and copy (25%), audience signal depth (25%), Shopping priority tiering logic (20%).
core_projects.independent_evidence: Exported TSV product feed file, GMC feed processing summary screenshot, and completed PMax asset workbook.
core_projects.reporting_requirements: E-Commerce Catalog & PMax Architecture Blueprint detailing priority tiering, asset matrix, and feed health SOPs.

core_projects.operational_mode: Meta Ads Manager Sandbox / Draft Mode (Zero Personal Ad Spend Required)
core_projects.business_brief: A fast-growing fintech brand offering investment advisory services and a companion subscription app requires a full-funnel paid acquisition strategy on Meta. The company needs one native Lead Generation campaign targeting prospective high-net-worth clients with qualified Instant Forms, and one Sales Acquisition campaign (Advantage+ Shopping / App) with a 3x3 creative testing matrix, customer budget caps, and strict audience exclusions.
core_projects.data_requirements: Client value proposition, target customer demographics, sample customer email lists (hashed), creative image/video raw assets, and compliance guidelines.
student_actions: Set up Meta Business Portfolio assets, configuring ad account permissions, custom conversion rules, and billing thresholds.
Construct a native Meta Instant Lead Form with qualifying questions to filter high-intent prospects from unqualified leads.
Configure a full-funnel ODAX campaign structure with broad prospecting, 1% lookalike tiers, and time-decay retargeting ad sets.
Apply strict audience exclusion rules to prevent serving prospecting ads to existing customers, active leads, and recent purchasers.
Build an Advantage+ Shopping Campaign with a 15% existing customer budget cap to enforce incremental new-user acquisition.
Design a complete 3x3 Creative Testing Matrix spanning 3 distinct marketing angles across 3 creative formats (UGC video, carousel, static feature callout).
exact_deliverables: Meta Ads Master Campaign Build Document (PDF/Doc) with targeting, budget, and bidding specifications.
High-Intent Native Instant Lead Form Specification with CRM webhook mapping.
Advantage+ Shopping Campaign Configuration with customer budget cap rules.
3x3 Creative Testing Matrix with ad copy, headline variations, and visual storyboard links.
core_projects.qa_requirements: Strict audience exclusions applied to all prospecting ad sets; Instant Form contains at least 2 custom qualifying questions; creative assets meet 1:1 and 9:16 aspect ratio specifications; zero policy-prohibited superlatives or financial claims.
core_projects.evaluation_rubric: Campaign architecture and audience exclusion rigor (30%), creative matrix depth and hook quality (30%), Advantage+ setup compliance (20%), budget optimization logic (20%).
core_projects.independent_evidence: Meta Ads Manager draft campaign export/screenshots, Instant Form preview links, and completed 3x3 creative deck.
core_projects.reporting_requirements: Meta Paid Acquisition Strategy Deck with audience breakdown, creative angles, and scaling criteria.

core_projects.operational_mode: Live Student Sandbox Website & GTM Preview Mode (Zero Paid Tooling Required)
core_projects.business_brief: An e-commerce retailer has suffered significant attribution loss and inaccurate conversion tracking due to browser ad blockers and misconfigured tags. The business requires a full-funnel client-side tracking architecture using Google Tag Manager, custom JavaScript dataLayer events, GA4 Key Event designation, and Google Ads Enhanced Conversions to establish reliable acquisition measurement.
core_projects.data_requirements: Sandbox e-commerce website access, event taxonomy documentation, Google Ads conversion action IDs, and GA4 measurement ID.
student_actions: Draft a comprehensive Event Tracking Plan spreadsheet mapping business milestones to standardized GA4 e-commerce events.
Implement JavaScript dataLayer.push() commands on the sandbox site for view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, and purchase.
Configure GTM User-Defined Variables to dynamically extract transaction ID, revenue, tax, shipping, and items array.
Deploy Google Ads Conversion Tracking with a sitewide Conversion Linker tag and configure Enhanced Conversions with hashed user data.
Verify tag firing order, event timing, and variable values in GTM Preview Mode (Tag Assistant) and GA4 DebugView.
Export the production GTM container JSON file and compile a verification log with annotated debugging screenshots.
exact_deliverables: Master Event Tracking Plan & Taxonomy Spreadsheet (.xlsx).
Exported Production GTM Container JSON file.
GA4 E-Commerce Events & Key Event Designation Verification Log.
Google Ads Enhanced Conversions Implementation Document.
Annotated Tag Assistant & DebugView Validation Dossier.
core_projects.qa_requirements: Zero unhandled JavaScript errors in console; Conversion Linker fires on all pages; GA4 purchase event contains required items array and transaction_id; Enhanced Conversions pass normalized, SHA-256 hashed user data.
core_projects.evaluation_rubric: dataLayer variable configuration and push mechanics (30%), Enhanced Conversions implementation (25%), GTM tag/trigger architecture (25%), Tag Assistant and DebugView verification rigor (20%).
core_projects.independent_evidence: Exported GTM container JSON file, live Tag Assistant session URL/log, and GA4 DebugView event stream screenshot.
core_projects.reporting_requirements: Technical Measurement Architecture Document with dataLayer specifications and QA sign-off checklist.

core_projects.operational_mode: Meta Events Manager Sandbox & Controlled Webhook Demonstration (Zero Paid Infrastructure Required)
core_projects.business_brief: A direct-to-consumer brand's Meta ad performance has degraded due to low Event Match Quality (EMQ) scores and browser-level tracking prevention. The brand needs an integrated tracking setup combining browser Meta Pixel with server-side Conversions API (CAPI), complete with event deduplication via matching Event IDs, to restore signal quality and optimize Advantage+ algorithmic bidding.
core_projects.data_requirements: Meta Pixel ID, CAPI access token (sandbox), student test website, and test event code from Meta Events Manager.
student_actions: Install Meta Pixel base code and standard event tags (ViewContent, AddToCart, Lead, Purchase) via GTM.
Implement a custom JavaScript variable in GTM generating a unique event_id timestamped string for every user interaction.
Configure both the browser Pixel tag and the simulated server CAPI payload to transmit identical event_name and event_id parameters.
Normalize and hash customer parameters (email, phone, city) to SHA-256 standards before transmission.
Verify event receipt, server-to-browser matching, and successful deduplication in Meta Events Manager Test Events tool.
Diagnose and remediate 3 common tracking flaws: missing currency parameters, duplicate un-deduplicated purchases, and low EMQ scores.
exact_deliverables: GTM Meta Pixel & CAPI Deduplication Container Configuration (JSON).
Meta Events Manager Test Events Log showing verified browser/server deduplication.
Event Match Quality (EMQ) Diagnostic Report with optimization scorecards.
Tracking Flaw Remediation Log with before/after diagnostic screenshots.
core_projects.qa_requirements: 100% of tested events demonstrate confirmed deduplication in Meta Events Manager; target EMQ score ≥ 8.0/10 for lead/purchase events; zero unhashed PII transmitted in browser payloads.
core_projects.evaluation_rubric: Event ID generation and deduplication architecture (35%), CAPI payload parameter completeness (25%), EMQ score optimization (25%), diagnostic troubleshooting rigor (15%).
core_projects.independent_evidence: Meta Events Manager Test Events session screenshot showing 'Browser / Server (Deduplicated)' status and exported GTM container JSON.
core_projects.reporting_requirements: Meta Signal Resilience & CAPI Deduplication Technical Report.

core_projects.project_title: Landing Page CRO and A/B Testing
core_projects.operational_mode: WordPress Sandbox, Microsoft Clarity & Simulated Behavioral Analytics (Zero Personal Ad Spend Required)
core_projects.business_brief: A high-growth B2B enterprise software company is running paid Google and Meta campaigns to a landing page with an underwhelming 1.8% lead conversion rate. The company needs an empirical heuristic CRO audit using the LIFT model, behavioral user analysis in Microsoft Clarity, an improved mobile-first landing page design, and a statistically sound A/B testing roadmap.
core_projects.data_requirements: Access to live landing page, 30 days of simulated Clarity behavioral data (heatmaps and 20 session recordings), and traffic volume metrics.
student_actions: Conduct a 20-point heuristic CRO audit using the 6-factor LIFT Model (Value Proposition, Relevance, Clarity, Urgency, Anxiety, Distraction).
Analyze Microsoft Clarity click heatmaps, scroll maps, and session recordings to isolate mobile rage clicks and form drop-off points.
Diagnose message match discrepancies between top-performing ad creative hooks and the landing page hero section.
Design a high-converting desktop and mobile landing page wireframe with sticky CTAs, social proof ribbons, and reduced form friction.
Formulate 2 testable conversion hypotheses and calculate required sample sizes, baseline conversion rates, and test durations for 95% statistical confidence.
Prioritize a backlog of 5 optimization test concepts using the PIE (Potential, Importance, Ease) framework.
exact_deliverables: 20-Point Heuristic CRO Audit Report (PDF) with annotated conversion friction points.
Microsoft Clarity Behavioral Analysis with heatmap and session replay insights.
Redesigned Mobile-First Landing Page Wireframe Specification (Canva/Figma).
Two Complete A/B Test Experiment Design Briefs with statistical sample size calculations.
PIE Prioritized Conversion Experiment Backlog.
core_projects.qa_requirements: Audit covers all 6 LIFT factors; wireframe includes dedicated mobile thumb-zone layout; sample size calculations account for 95% confidence and 80% statistical power; zero unscientific 'instant conversion doubling' claims.
core_projects.evaluation_rubric: Depth of heuristic CRO analysis (35%), Clarity behavioral diagnosis (25%), A/B hypothesis scientific rigor and sample size calculation (25%), Wireframe UX clarity (15%).
core_projects.independent_evidence: Annotated audit PDF, Clarity heatmap screenshot evidence, completed wireframe link, and sample size calculator export.
core_projects.reporting_requirements: Executive CRO Audit & Experimentation Roadmap presentation.

best_practices: Never scale paid ad spend into a store with unresolved mobile checkout friction or unverified feed diagnostics.
Optimize for Contribution Margin and Profit on Ad Spend (POAS) rather than relying solely on vanity platform ROAS.
Structure Performance Max asset groups strictly by product category with first-party audience signals.
Enforce existing customer budget caps on Meta Advantage+ campaigns to ensure genuine incremental customer acquisition.
Maintain strict email deliverability authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and automated sunset policies.

Treating platform-reported ROAS as true profitability without accounting for COGS, shipping, payment gateway fees, and returns.

faq.question: Who is the E-Commerce & Growth Marketing Specialist program designed for?
faq.answer: This course is specifically engineered for D2C founders, Shopify store owners, performance marketers, digital marketing professionals, agency growth managers, and freelancers who want to specialize in high-growth online retail marketing.

faq.question: What are the prerequisites for this course?
faq.answer: Learners should have basic digital marketing literacy, familiarity with web browsing, spreadsheets, and commercial business terminology. Prior exposure to Google Ads, Meta Ads, or basic store operations is helpful but not required. No coding or web development experience is necessary.

faq.question: How is this course different from the AI Digital Marketing Specialist and AI Digital Marketing Strategist programs?
faq.answer: The AI Digital Marketing Specialist (3 Months, 120h, ₹24,900) is a foundational execution program covering general SEO, social, and search ads. The AI Digital Marketing Strategist (6 Months, 240h, ₹44,900) is an executive career mastery in enterprise omnichannel strategy, technical SEO/GEO, and marketing automation. The E-Commerce & Growth Marketing Specialist (4 Months, 160h, ₹34,900) is an intensive, specialized vertical program focused 100% on online retail: Shopify store architecture, Google Merchant Center feed diagnostics, Google Shopping & PMax, Meta Advantage+ Catalog ads, CRO, Klaviyo retention, and e-commerce unit economics.

faq.question: What is the total duration and guided training hours?
faq.answer: The program spans 4 Months (16 Weeks) comprising exactly 160 guided training hours led by industry instructors, plus an estimated 60-80 recommended hours for independent store building, feed diagnostics, and project development.

faq.question: What is the fee structure for the E-Commerce & Growth Marketing Specialist program?
faq.answer: The total tuition fee is ₹34,900 INR (taxes/GST extra where applicable). Flexible monthly EMI options are available to make enrollment accessible.

faq.question: Do students need an active paid Shopify subscription or advertising budget to participate?
faq.answer: No. All hands-on training is conducted using free Shopify Partner development stores, sandbox accounts, Google Merchant Center test environments, draft-mode ad managers, and platform sandbox environments. Students do not need personal ad spend or paid store subscriptions.

faq.question: Will students work on real-world e-commerce stores and datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. Students audit and build real sandbox stores, optimize 50+ SKU product feeds, troubleshoot simulated Merchant Center policy disapprovals, analyze real e-commerce GA4 and Google Ads datasets, and build live Looker Studio dashboards.

faq.question: Which specific e-commerce platforms and ad networks are covered in depth?
faq.answer: Primary platforms covered include Shopify, Google Merchant Center, Google Ads (Standard Shopping, Performance Max, Demand Gen), Meta Ads Manager (Commerce Manager, Advantage+ Catalog Ads), Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Klaviyo, Brevo, and Microsoft Clarity.

faq.question: How is Google Merchant Center and Product Feed training delivered?
faq.answer: Students learn end-to-end feed architecture: primary vs. supplemental feeds, Google Product Taxonomy, structured title engineering, attribute compliance (GTIN, MPN, brand), shipping/tax rules, and diagnostic error remediation for account disapprovals.

faq.question: What kind of retention marketing and lifecycle automation will I learn?
faq.answer: You will master e-commerce retention using Klaviyo and Brevo: Welcome Series, Abandoned Cart/Checkout recovery, Post-Purchase upsells, Customer Winback, RFM customer segmentation, and compliance-first SMS marketing.

faq.question: How does AI fit into this e-commerce curriculum?
faq.answer: AI is integrated throughout: using AI for product catalog enrichment, generating compelling product descriptions, creating multi-angle direct response ad copy, designing visual ad creatives and video storyboards, and conducting competitor intelligence.

faq.question: What portfolio deliverables and capstone projects will I complete?
faq.answer: You will complete 8 comprehensive portfolio assets, culminating in a 90-Day Full-Funnel E-Commerce Growth Strategy and client pitch deck that demonstrates end-to-end store optimization, ad architecture, and retention capability.

faq.question: Does Nova Skills guarantee job placement or e-commerce revenue upon graduation?
faq.answer: Nova Skills provides dedicated placement support, portfolio defense training, resume engineering, and interview preparation, but does NOT make false or deceptive job or revenue guarantees. Success depends on the learner's skill execution and market performance.

modules.title: E-Commerce Business Models, Unit Economics & Customer Journey
modules.summary: Master the commercial fundamentals of online retail: business models, contribution margin modeling, CAC-to-LTV ratios, and multi-touch customer buying journeys.
modules.why_it_matters: Scaling an e-commerce store without clear unit economics and margin awareness inevitably leads to unprofitable ad spend and cash-flow failure.

lessons.title: E-Commerce Business Models: D2C, B2B, Marketplaces & Hybrid Operations
topics: Comparison of Direct-to-Consumer (D2C), marketplace retail (Amazon, Flipkart), and hybrid multichannel models
Inventory-holding vs. on-demand manufacturing and dropshipping unit economic differences
Private label branding strategies and value chain positioning for sustainable pricing power
learning_objectives: Differentiate core retail business models and identify operational margin trade-offs
Evaluate brand defensibility and margin potential across distinct e-commerce categories

lessons.title: E-Commerce Financials: COGS, Contribution Margins & Profit on Ad Spend (POAS)
topics: Deconstructing the P&L: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), payment gateway fees, pick-pack-ship costs, and returns
Calculating Contribution Margin 1 (gross), Contribution Margin 2 (post-shipping/packaging), and Contribution Margin 3 (post-ad spend)
Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) limitations vs. Profit on Ad Spend (POAS) and Marketing Efficiency Ratio (MER)
learning_objectives: Build an e-commerce unit economics model in Google Sheets factoring in all fulfillment and marketing expenses
Establish break-even ROAS targets based on category-specific gross and net margins

lessons.title: Customer Economics: AOV, CAC, Customer Lifetime Value & Cohort Retention
topics: Average Order Value (AOV) optimization levers: bundles, thresholds, and cross-sells
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) blended vs. first-touch calculation and payback period benchmarks
Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) forecasting, 30/60/90-day cohort retention curves, and repeat purchase frequency
learning_objectives: Calculate realistic LTV:CAC ratios and determine sustainable payback periods for funded and bootstrapped brands
Identify early warning signs of cohort decay in customer retention spreadsheets

lessons.title: The Modern E-Commerce Customer Journey: TOFU Discovery to BOFU Loyalty
topics: Omnichannel customer path: social discovery, search intent, remarketing touchpoints, and email reactivation
Micro-conversions across the buying funnel: product impressions, clicks, cart adds, and checkout initiations
Mapping post-purchase touchpoints: transactional alerts, unboxing experience, review requests, and referral triggers
learning_objectives: Map an end-to-end e-commerce customer buying journey across paid, owned, and earned media touchpoints
