Technical on-page SEO: custom meta titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, and Open Graph social preview cards
Web accessibility in Framer: semantic HTML tags (nav, main, section, footer), image alt text, and color contrast
Framer Agents 2026 workflow: using AI prompts for rapid section scaffolding, content translation, and SEO recommendations
Framer MCP architectural exposure: understanding the October 22, 2026 Model Context Protocol integration for AI agent collaboration
Production deployment: publishing to live `.framer.media` domain, testing live cross-browser performance, and client handoff
lessons.why_it_matters: A website that cannot be found by search engines, fails accessibility audits, or cannot receive contact submissions has zero commercial utility. Professional publishing requires rigorous SEO, functional form validation, and clean hosting deployment.
lessons.what_learner_does: Configure a working contact form with success/error states, set up full SEO and Open Graph metadata, run an accessibility audit, explore Framer Agents for layout assistance, and publish the live site on `.framer.media`.
lessons.expected_outcome: A published, live, accessible marketing website on `.framer.media` featuring working forms, verified SEO tags, and responsive layouts across all viewports.
lessons.example: Publishing `https://novaskills-student-portfolio.framer.media`, validating that submitting the contact form sends an instant notification email, and verifying the Open Graph preview card appears perfectly on LinkedIn and Twitter.

modules.hands_on_practice: Build a complete, responsive multi-page marketing website in Framer from a researched Figma design: homepage, features page, CMS-powered case studies, working contact form, scroll interactions, and live publication.
modules.assignment: Deliver a Live Framer Production Package containing: (1) Editable Framer project link, (2) Live accessible `.framer.media` website URL, (3) Verified responsive navigation demonstrating desktop-to-mobile drawer switching, (4) Populated CMS collection with 5 records, (5) Working contact form test receipt, and (6) Complete SEO & Accessibility Audit Report.
modules.business_application: Deliver high-converting, live production websites directly to clients without hiring frontend web developers, enabling graduates to command $2,000–$5,000+ for freelance website builds.
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 07 major production deliverable: a live, responsive, CMS-driven marketing website deployed to production.

modules.module_title: Generative AI for UX, UI & Product Design
modules.module_purpose: Demystify generative AI in modern product design, establishing disciplined, ethical, and highly effective workflows where AI accelerates research synthesis, microcopy exploration, and visual scaffolding while preserving strict human authorship and decision-making rigor.
what_you_will_learn: Leverage Large Language Models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) for qualitative research synthesis and discussion guide scaffolding.
Generate contextual, humanized UI microcopy (empty states, error messages, onboarding tooltips) across diverse brand tones.
Utilize Figma AI and Figma Make for rapid wireframe exploration, layer auto-renaming, and synthetic prototype scaffolding.
Direct Framer AI and Agents for layout section ideation while manually refactoring outputs into accessible components.
Synthesize hero visual assets using Adobe Firefly with controlled prompt engineering and C2PA provenance credentials.
Enforce strict ethical boundaries, detecting AI hallucinations, preventing synthetic research fabrication, and auditing WCAG 2.2 contrast.
key_concepts: Prompt Engineering for UX Research & Synthesis
Figma Make: AI Prototyping Boundaries & Manual Fallbacks
WCAG Accessibility Auditing on AI-Generated Palettes

lessons.lesson_title: Prompt Architecture for UX Research, Problem Discovery & Synthesis
lessons.what_is_taught: The role of AI in modern product design: separating practical productivity gains from marketing hype. Prompt engineering architectures (Role, Context, Task, Constraints, Output Format) for drafting interview guides, stakeholder surveys, and competitive heuristic matrices. Using LLMs to synthesize raw qualitative interview transcripts into thematic summaries while strictly preventing synthetic research fabrication.
subtopics: The 2026 AI product design ecosystem: LLMs, multimodal vision models, and in-canvas AI copilots
Prompt engineering for UX researchers: establishing Role, Context, Task, Constraints, and Examples (Few-Shot)
Drafting qualitative discussion guides and screening surveys using structured prompt templates
Synthesizing raw user interview transcripts: extracting pain points, mental models, and recurring quotes
Detecting AI hallucinations: cross-referencing AI summaries against verbatim interview recordings
Ethical boundary enforcement: why generating 'synthetic user research' or fake personas destroys product integrity
Authoring data-grounded How-Might-We statements and UX hypotheses with AI brainstorming assistance
lessons.why_it_matters: AI is an extraordinary research scaffolding assistant, but a dangerous substitute for real users. Grounding AI in empirical human data prevents costly product failures caused by algorithmic hallucinations.
lessons.what_learner_does: Author a structured prompt recipe to summarize 3 raw interview transcripts, audit the AI output against source notes, eliminate 2 hallucinated assumptions, and formulate 3 verified HMW problem statements.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented AI Research Prompt Log and an audited, human-verified qualitative research summary table.
lessons.example: Using ChatGPT to cluster 25 raw interview notes into 4 themes, then verifying that every clustered insight links directly to an actual timestamped user quote from the research dossier.

lessons.lesson_title: AI-Powered UX Writing, Content Strategy & Microcopy Ideation
lessons.what_is_taught: Leveraging generative AI for interface microcopy and UX writing. Generating contextual copy variations for complex interface states: onboarding tooltips, permission dialogs, form validation errors, empty states, and payment failure recovery. Establishing tone of voice matrices (Friendly, Technical, Urgent, Reassuring) and checking copy for plain language readability and localization expansion.
subtopics: Interface microcopy foundations: clarity, brevity, purpose, and reducing cognitive anxiety
Establishing tone of voice matrices: configuring prompts for casual consumer apps vs enterprise FinTech platforms
Generating edge-case UI copy: server timeouts, expired sessions, payment declines, and empty search results
Form microcopy: persistent input labels, helper text, inline validation hints, and error correction prompts
Accessibility in UX writing: writing descriptive link text, screen-reader alt text, and plain language standards
Localization readiness: testing microcopy variations against language character expansion (e.g. German, French)
A/B copy testing ideation: generating 5 distinct CTA button hypotheses for conversion optimization
lessons.why_it_matters: Poorly phrased error messages cause instant user frustration and cart abandonment. AI enables designers to rapidly explore dozens of contextual copy variations and stress-test communication across complex edge cases.
lessons.what_learner_does: Generate and refine 15 contextual microcopy snippets for a multi-step checkout flow (covering error states, empty cart, and security reassurance) across two distinct brand tones.
lessons.expected_outcome: A comprehensive UX Microcopy Matrix containing error, empty, and confirmation copy with plain-language readability scores.
lessons.example: Refining a blunt error message 'Card Declined: Error 402' into a reassuring, actionable microcopy: 'Your bank declined this transaction. Please check your card details or try a different payment method.'

lessons.lesson_title: In-Canvas Generative UI: Figma AI, Figma Make & Framer Agents
lessons.what_is_taught: In-canvas generative AI tools: Figma AI (prompt-to-wireframe, layer auto-renaming, visual asset search, synthetic realistic data insertion). Operational boundaries of Figma Make for AI component prototyping, noting seat/tier dependencies and mastering manual Auto Layout fallbacks. Framer Agents: generative section ideation, responsive layout translation, and refactoring raw AI output into accessible Auto Layout frames.
subtopics: Figma AI in-canvas capabilities: automatic layer renaming, visual asset search, and realistic data population
Prompt-to-wireframe exploration: generating initial layout concepts and assessing structural viability
Figma Make mechanics: exploring AI-assisted component prototyping while maintaining manual component fallback skills
Framer Agents: utilizing AI for rapid page section scaffolding, responsive layout translation, and CMS drafting
The 'Human-in-the-Loop' refactoring protocol: breaking down chaotic AI groups into rigid Auto Layout containers
Binding AI-generated components to certified design system variables and typography tokens
Generating visual hero assets in Adobe Firefly and inspecting C2PA Content Credentials provenance metadata
lessons.why_it_matters: Raw AI layouts are notoriously brittle: they contain unorganized layers, arbitrary pixel values, and zero design token bindings. Professional designers treat AI output as raw scaffolding that must be manually engineered into production code.
lessons.what_learner_does: Generate a landing page hero section using Framer AI / Figma AI, inspect its flaws, refactor the layout into strict Auto Layout containers, bind it to design tokens, and document the before/after refactoring diff.
lessons.expected_outcome: A side-by-side comparison file demonstrating the transformation of a raw AI generation into an accessible, tokenized, responsive UI component.
lessons.example: Taking an AI-generated card with fixed 380px width and broken layer names ('Frame 142'), renaming layers semantically, applying Auto Layout with Fill Container, and binding colors to `surface-card` tokens.

lessons.lesson_title: Responsible AI Product Design, Bias Auditing & Human Oversight
lessons.what_is_taught: Ethical product design in the age of generative AI: identifying systemic training bias in image and text models, preventing demographic erasure, and validating WCAG 2.2 accessibility on AI-suggested color palettes. Intellectual property, licensing, data privacy, and user consent. Authoring an authoritative AI Disclosure Statement for client and portfolio transparency.
subtopics: Algorithmic bias and representation risks: identifying stereotypes in AI-generated imagery and user persona drafts
Data privacy and corporate security: handling sensitive user data and proprietary client IP with cloud AI models
Copyright and commercial licensing: understanding generative AI training sets, commercial indemnification, and C2PA
Automated accessibility auditing: scanning AI-suggested color combinations for WCAG 2.2 contrast failures
User trust and transparency: designing clear user notifications when AI is driving interface recommendations
The Nova Skills Human Authorship Standard: establishing mandatory human oversight and editing protocols
Authoring an AI Transparency & Provenance Dossier for professional portfolio presentation
lessons.why_it_matters: Deploying unvetted AI designs exposes businesses to severe legal liability, copyright infringement, and public accessibility scandals. Ethical AI literacy establishes graduates as trustworthy, responsible design leaders.
lessons.what_learner_does: Conduct a comprehensive ethical and accessibility audit on an AI-assisted design project, remediate 3 contrast/bias violations, and author a formal AI Transparency Statement.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented AI Ethics & Accessibility Audit report featuring verified WCAG compliance and a signed Human Authorship disclosure.
lessons.example: Auditing an AI-generated palette that proposed light gray text (#94A3B8) on a white background (failing contrast at 2.3:1), and adjusting it to slate gray (#475569) to achieve a certified 4.6:1 WCAG AA pass.

modules.hands_on_practice: Execute an AI-assisted product design sprint: compare manual design workflows with AI scaffolding (ChatGPT, Figma AI, Framer Agents), audit outputs, refactor into accessible Auto Layout, and document human oversight.
modules.assignment: Deliver an AI-Augmented Product Design Dossier containing: (1) Prompt engineering logs used for discovery and microcopy, (2) Raw AI wireframe versus manually refactored Figma component comparison, (3) Live Framer section generated and styled with Framer Agents, and (4) An executive Human Oversight & Ethics Audit certifying authentic research and WCAG 2.2 compliance.
modules.business_application: Accelerate design discovery and iteration cycles by up to 3x while strictly eliminating legal, copyright, and accessibility risks through rigorous human-in-the-loop validation.
modules.expected_outcome: Verified completion of Module 08 demonstrating advanced prompt engineering, layout refactoring, and ethical AI governance in product design.

modules.module_title: Product Thinking, UX Metrics & Team Collaboration
modules.module_purpose: Transition designers from craft specialists into strategic product partners, teaching them how to evaluate product health through actionable UX metrics, align design initiatives with business KPIs, and collaborate seamlessly across cross-functional agile teams.
what_you_will_learn: Align design decisions with commercial business models (SaaS, marketplace, freemium, transactional).
Apply quantitative UX measurement frameworks, specifically Google HEART and System Usability Scale (SUS).
Analyze conversion funnels, identify drop-off inflection points, and formulate data-driven A/B test hypotheses.
Collaborate effectively within the Product Trio (Product Manager, Lead Designer, Engineering Lead) using Agile/Scrum.

lessons.lesson_title: Product Business Models, Unit Economics & The Google HEART Framework
lessons.what_is_taught: Product thinking fundamentals: user outcomes vs feature output, digital business models (B2B SaaS recurring subscriptions, two-sided marketplaces, consumer e-commerce), and key commercial metrics (Customer Acquisition Cost [CAC], Lifetime Value [LTV], Churn). The Google HEART framework (Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, Task Success) and translating abstract business goals into measurable UX KPIs.
subtopics: Product thinking mental model: shifting focus from designing outputs (features) to achieving outcomes (user value)
Digital product business models: understanding unit economics, SaaS ARR/MRR, marketplace takes, and transaction fees
Key business metrics: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), Lifetime Value (LTV), Churn Rate, and Monthly Active Users (MAU)
The Google HEART framework deep dive: Goals, Signals, and Metrics across Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, Task Success
System Usability Scale (SUS) benchmarks: interpreting usability scores and correlating SUS with customer retention
Mapping business goals to user pain points: identifying commercial opportunities within user journeys
Formulating testable design hypotheses: 'We believe that by [doing X], [user group] will achieve [outcome Y], as measured by [metric Z]'
lessons.why_it_matters: Designers who only discuss aesthetics are treated as pixel-pushers. Designers who speak the language of business metrics, CAC/LTV, and the HEART framework earn a seat at the executive decision-making table.
lessons.what_learner_does: Deconstruct the business model of an existing SaaS or subscription app, establish a complete Google HEART measurement matrix, and define 3 prioritized product success metrics.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented Product Strategy Canvas mapping user experience goals to business KPIs and Google HEART metrics.
lessons.example: Translating an executive goal of 'Increase revenue by 15%' into a concrete UX initiative: 'Improve checkout funnel task completion rate from 62% to 78% by introducing single-click mobile wallet authentication.'

lessons.lesson_title: Funnel Analytics, Agile Sprints & Cross-Functional Collaboration
lessons.what_is_taught: Conversion funnel analysis: diagnosing drop-off bottlenecks in onboarding and checkout flows. Agile product delivery rituals: sprint planning, daily standups, backlog grooming, and retrospective critiques. Collaborating inside the Product Trio (PM, Designer, Engineer), authoring user stories with clear acceptance criteria, and maintaining Design Decision Logs.
subtopics: Conversion funnel anatomy: step-by-step drop-off analysis and identifying friction choke points
Behavioral analytics tools overview: interpreting session recordings, scroll depth, and event drop-offs in Microsoft Clarity
The Product Trio dynamic: negotiating technical constraints with engineers and feature scope with product managers
Agile/Scrum workflows: sprint cycles, kanban boards, design backlogs, and story point estimation
Authoring developer-ready user stories: 'As a [user], I want to [action], so that [business benefit]'
Defining strict acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then) covering edge cases and error states
Maintaining Design Decision Logs: documenting rationale, trade-offs, and rejected alternatives for stakeholders
Leading stakeholder design reviews: handling constructive criticism and presenting evidence-based trade-offs
lessons.why_it_matters: The best design in the world is useless if engineers cannot build it within sprint timelines or if product managers deprioritize it. Strong collaboration and clear user stories ensure designs are built as intended.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyze real drop-off funnel data from a mobile subscription flow, identify the primary drop-off screen, write 2 developer user stories with acceptance criteria, and create a Design Decision Log entry.
lessons.expected_outcome: A Funnel Optimization Brief containing drop-off diagnostic analysis, developer user stories with acceptance criteria, and an annotated Design Decision Log.
lessons.example: Writing an acceptance criterion: 'Given a user enters an invalid promo code, When they tap Apply, Then the input field displays a red border, inline text reads Promo code not found, and the Checkout CTA remains disabled.'

Transforming raw files into an engaging visual narrative.

Structuring the case study narrative: Problem, Role, Timeline, Discovery, IA, Wireframes, Testing, Final UI, and Impact
The STAR methodology in design documentation: framing concrete commercial situations and measurable results

lessons.what_learner_does: Author an exhaustive, publication-ready case study for their primary capstone project, structuring problem framing, research evidence, iteration loops, usability testing metrics, and final Figma/Framer visuals.

Curating Behance and Dribbble showcases: formatting 1920x1080px presentation boards for visual design discoverability
Cold outreach strategy: crafting targeted, professional direct messages to design managers and recruitment partners

lessons.why_it_matters: Beautiful design files will never be seen if your resume is rejected by automated ATS screening filters. A clean, metrics-driven resume paired with an optimized LinkedIn profile ensures you consistently secure initial recruiter interviews.
lessons.what_learner_does: Typeset a 1-page ATS-compliant product designer resume in Figma/Word, optimize their LinkedIn headline and featured projects, and author a customized recruiter outreach message.
lessons.expected_outcome: A verified 1-page ATS-friendly PDF resume and an optimized, fully populated professional LinkedIn presence.
lessons.example: Transforming a weak resume bullet 'Designed mobile screens in Figma' into a powerful accomplishment: 'Architected a 10-component responsive UI kit in Figma with Auto Layout v5, cutting design-to-development handoff turnaround by 35%.'

modules.title: Design & Photoshop Foundations
modules.objective: Build a strong foundation in Photoshop's workspace, raster artwork, document preparation, image resolution and essential design principles.
topics: Photoshop interface and workspace customization: Tools panel, Options bar, Panels docking, and custom studio workspaces
Document creation, canvas dimensions, pixel aspect ratios, and resolution standards for web, screen, and print
Raster versus vector graphics: mathematical vectors vs pixel matrices, scalability boundaries, and interpolation artifacts
Common raster formats: PSD master working files, JPEG compression algorithms, PNG transparency, and WebP efficiency
Image resolution versus physical print dimensions: Pixels Per Inch (PPI) fundamentals and viewing distance calculation
Color modes: RGB additive color vs CMYK subtractive color, bit depth (8-bit vs 16-bit), and gamut limitations
Color profiles: sRGB for web outputs, Adobe RGB (1998) for wide-gamut workflows, and CMYK prepress target profiles
Core commercial design principles: visual hierarchy, contrast, balance, alignment, proximity, repetition, and purposeful whitespace
Advertising typography fundamentals: font pairing, tracking, leading, kerning, type hierarchy, and legibility over complex backgrounds
Layer fundamentals: background layer unlocking, layer stacking order, opacity vs fill, layer locking modes, and color coding
Transformation and alignment: Free Transform controls, proportional scaling, reference points, Skew, Distort, and Perspective
Rulers, guides, grids, and Smart Guides: precision coordinate positioning and mathematical margin setup
Artboards in Photoshop: multi-canvas setup for social media formats and responsive banner suites
Cropping and composition: Rule of Thirds, Golden Ratio, Straighten tool, and non-destructive crop modes
Studio asset sourcing, moodboard development, file naming conventions, and interpreting commercial design briefs
modules.hands_on_practice: Configure custom commercial workspaces; construct grid-aligned advertising canvases with designated margins and safe zones; balance typographic headlines over product photography with purposeful contrast.

assignment.title: Commercial Visual Layout Fundamentals
assignment.description: Create a clean promotional advertising layout using a supplied product photograph, brand headline, supporting copy, CTA button, brand color palette, and mathematical guides with strictly organized layer groups.
deliverables: Master layered editable PSD file with structured layer groups
Correct canvas settings (1080 × 1350 px, 72 PPI, sRGB color profile)
High-contrast visual hierarchy and aligned typography
Exported high-quality PNG and compressed JPEG preview files
Short 200-word design rationale explaining typographic and compositional choices

modules.assessment_criteria: Precision of canvas geometry, mathematical alignment with guides, readability of typographic hierarchy, proper color profile assignment, and clean layer naming.

modules.title: Precision Editing
modules.objective: Develop precise, controlled image-editing skills using selections, masks, paths, adjustment layers and Smart Objects.
topics: Selection fundamentals: Geometric Marquee tools, Lasso, Polygonal Lasso, and Magnetic Lasso mechanics
AI-assisted selection tools: Quick Selection, Object Selection Tool, Selection Brush, Magic Wand, and Select Subject engine
Select and Mask dedicated workspace: Global Refinements (Smooth, Feather, Contrast, Shift Edge) and View Modes
Refine Edge Brush: soft-edge isolation, fur and flyaway hair extraction, and edge contamination decontaminate colors
Non-destructive masking: Layer Masks vs permanent pixel deletion, revealing (white), concealing (black), and gray opacity gradients
Clipping masks: bounding adjustment layers and textures strictly to underlying shapes and text layers
Vector masks and Pen Tool mastery: Bézier curves, anchor points, smooth vs corner points, and Path Operations (Add, Subtract, Intersect)
Precision product clipping paths: creating ultra-sharp commercial vector silhouetting for e-commerce catalog isolation
Non-destructive Adjustment Layers: Levels histograms, input/output sliders, black/white/gray eyedroppers, and tonal clipping
Curves deep dive: S-curves for contrast, individual RGB channel curve color grading, and precise point sampling
Color adjustments: Hue/Saturation colorized modes, Color Balance shadow/midtone/highlight grading, Selective Color, and Vibrance
Adobe Camera Raw as a filter: white balance temperature/tint, exposure, highlight recovery, shadow boosting, clarity, and dehaze
Smart Objects architecture: Embedded vs Linked Smart Objects, preserving raw pixel data against destructive degradation
Smart Filters: applying reversible blurs, sharpening, and distortions with independent filter masks
Photoshop Blend Modes: Multiply (darken), Screen (lighten), Overlay/Soft Light (contrast), and Color/Luminosity separation
Layer Effects (Layer Styles): Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow, Stroke, Color Overlay, and Bevel & Emboss with non-destructive control
Quality assurance at 100% and 200% zoom: checking for fringing, halos, jagged edges, and mask bleed
modules.hands_on_practice: Hand-draw vector clipping paths around intricate product contours; isolate models with complex flyaway hair; perform non-destructive color balancing and tone curve corrections without modifying background pixels.

assignment.title: Precision Product Cutout & Color Correction
assignment.description: Isolate a complex product featuring reflective metallic, transparent glass, or intricate textured edges from a busy background. Apply non-destructive adjustment layers and Camera Raw filtering inside a Smart Object workflow.
deliverables: Original unedited source photograph
Isolated product on transparent background with sub-pixel edge refinement
Vector Pen Tool clipping path saved within the PSD Paths panel
Non-destructive Curves, Levels, and Selective Color adjustment layers
Organized PSD working file with Smart Objects and zero destructive pixel edits
High-resolution transparent PNG export and quality inspection checklist

modules.assessment_criteria: Absence of background halos, edge smoothness and accuracy, preservation of fine hair/details, reversible non-destructive layer stack, and histogram balance.

modules.title: Retouching & Image Enhancement
modules.objective: Learn to enhance portraits and products while preserving realistic texture, lighting, geometry and visual authenticity.
topics: Professional retouching philosophy: enhancement vs alteration, visual authenticity, and client brief adherence
Before-and-after image evaluation: identifying sensor dust, scratches, stray hairs, blemishes, and tonal inconsistencies
Healing toolset: Spot Healing Brush (Content-Aware, Proximity Match), Healing Brush (sampled texture), and Patch Tool
The Remove Tool (AI-powered generative cleanup): clearing complex background distractions while reconstructing underlying textures
Clone Stamp Tool: sample alignment, brush hardness, opacity/flow settings, and avoiding repeating stamp patterns
Frequency separation fundamentals: separating high-frequency texture from low-frequency color and tone, and understanding over-smoothing risks
Dodge and Burn techniques: non-destructive 50% gray overlay layers, Curves-based dodging and burning, and sculpting facial/product volume
Portrait retouching ethics: preserving natural skin pores, correcting temporary blemishes without plasticized smoothing
Commercial product retouching: removing manufacturing seam lines, packaging scratches, label misalignments, and dust specks
Challenging surface materials: glass transparency preservation, chrome/metallic reflection cleanup, and matte surface smoothing
Product label preservation: maintaining brand logos, regulatory text, and barcode clarity without blur or distortion
Realistic shadow anatomy: contact shadows (darkest, tight), cast shadows (directional, softening), and ambient occlusion
Shadow creation and rendering: custom brush softness, motion blurs, perspective skews, and opacity gradients matching original light sources
Realistic reflections: duplicating subjects, vertical inversion, perspective warping, layer masking gradients, and surface texture blending
Perspective correction: Perspective Warp tool, Lens Correction filter for optical barrel/pincushion distortion, and vertical line straightening
Camera Raw finishing: detail sharpening, luminance noise reduction, chromatic aberration removal, and output sharpening
Image quality inspection: 100% zoom check for retouching artifacts, banding, edge halos, and color blotches
modules.hands_on_practice: Clean up cosmetic packaging imperfections; reconstruct broken reflections on chrome and glass surfaces; build multi-layer contact and cast shadows matching a studio strobe key light; execute ethical portrait skin cleanup.

assignment.title: Commercial Product Retouching Before/After Series

deliverables: Three high-resolution original source photographs
Three professionally retouched commercial master images
Side-by-side before/after comparison presentation sheets
Documented evidence of natural skin/product texture preservation at 200% zoom
Realistic hand-rendered contact and cast shadow layers
Three editable, fully organized PSD files demonstrating non-destructive workflows
Completed commercial retouching quality assurance checklist

competencies: Remove Tool and Clone Stamp proficiency
Realistic contact and cast shadow construction
modules.assessment_criteria: Complete removal of surface flaws, natural preservation of micro-textures without plastic blur, physical realism of constructed shadows, and editable PSD layer cleanliness.

modules.title: Commercial Compositing & AI
modules.objective: Build photorealistic commercial composites using traditional Photoshop craftsmanship and AI-assisted tools where appropriate.
topics: Commercial compositing principles: visual storytelling, concept ideation, and moodboard construction
Source asset compatibility: camera focal length, sensor resolution, perspective angles, horizon line, and eye-level alignment
Lighting consistency: identifying key light, fill light, rim light, ambient bounce, and color temperature (Kelvin) across sources
Scale, proportion, and spatial placement: establishing realistic physical relationships between products and environments
Atmospheric depth: aerial perspective, contrast falloff with distance, depth-of-field simulation, and Gaussian/Lens Blur gradients
Edge blending: hair and transparent object integration, light wrap simulation via inner shadows and brush overlays
Color grading for compositing: Curves matching highlights, midtones, and shadows to the environment's ambient color palette
Generative Fill in commercial workflows: adding contextual background environments, extending sets, and replacing unwanted props
Generative Expand: expanding composition canvases to accommodate new aspect ratios and white space requirements
Harmonize tool mechanics: matching lighting, color balance, and tonal contrast between cutout foregrounds and background plates
Supported Harmonize workflows: layer rasterization requirements, Smart Object conversion constraints, and manual refinement
Generate Background: creating contextual concept environments with Adobe Firefly generative models
Prompt engineering for commercial image editing: descriptive keywords, lighting terminology, lens specifications, and avoiding prompt drift
AI artifact identification: spotting anatomical errors, perspective mismatches, distorted text/logos, unnatural shadows, and edge melting
Manual correction of AI outputs: stamping over AI artifacts, manual edge masking, repainting textures, and replacing distorted logos
Adobe licensing and commercial terms: generative credits consumption, commercial-use terms, beta limitations, and client copyright
Stock asset licensing, model releases, and property permissions for commercial advertising deployment
modules.hands_on_practice: Place an e-commerce product photograph into an AI-generated luxury lifestyle environment; adjust lighting angle and color temperature with Curves; cast contact and directional shadows; paint light wrap along product boundaries; fix melted AI background details with manual cloning.

faq.question: What is Adobe Photoshop — Commercial Image Editing & Design?
faq.answer: Adobe Photoshop — Commercial Image Editing & Design is an intensive 6-week, 48-hour certification programme focused on practical, commercial-grade raster editing, high-end product/portrait retouching, photorealistic compositing, advertising art direction, and multi-format campaign production. Learners master precision tools, non-destructive editing, Adobe Camera Raw, and Adobe Firefly AI features while building a portfolio of client-ready artwork backed by organized, editable PSD files.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The course begins with foundational concepts in Photoshop's workspace, pixels, resolution, color modes (RGB vs CMYK), and basic design principles before advancing systematically through precision masking, retouching, compositing, and advertising production. No prior Photoshop experience is required, though general computer literacy and familiarity with digital images are helpful.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is exactly 6 Weeks (48 total learning hours), priced at a transparent institutional fee of ₹6,900 (plus applicable 18% GST). Nova Skills follows a strict Truth in Pricing policy with zero artificial countdown discounts or inflated comparison prices.

faq.question: Will I learn photo editing and retouching?
faq.answer: Yes, extensive practical photo editing and retouching are core pillars of the curriculum. You will learn to use the Remove Tool, Healing Brush, Spot Healing Brush, Clone Stamp, frequency separation concepts, and Dodge & Burn techniques to clean blemishes, remove distractions, and sculpt light while preserving authentic skin and surface micro-textures.

faq.question: Does the course cover product photo editing?
faq.answer: Yes. Product photo editing is heavily emphasized, covering dust and scratch removal, packaging cleanup, metallic and glass reflection management, label preservation, and hand-rendering realistic contact and cast shadows for e-commerce and commercial print catalogs.

faq.question: Will I learn advanced selections and masking?
faq.answer: Yes. You will master geometric marquees, Lasso tools, Object Selection, Select Subject, and the dedicated Select and Mask workspace. You will also learn sub-pixel hair extraction, Refine Edge techniques, Layer Masks, clipping masks, and the Pen Tool for precision vector clipping paths.

faq.question: What is non-destructive editing?
faq.answer: Non-destructive editing is a professional workflow where original image pixels are never permanently deleted or degraded. By utilizing Layer Masks, non-destructive Adjustment Layers (Curves, Levels, Color Balance), Smart Objects, and Smart Filters, any edit can be modified, re-adjusted, or reverted at any point in the future.

faq.question: Will I learn Adobe Camera Raw?
faq.answer: Yes. Adobe Camera Raw is integrated as an essential supporting tool. You will learn raw exposure balancing, white balance temperature/tint adjustments, highlight recovery, shadow opening, clarity, dehaze, chromatic aberration removal, and selective color grading.

faq.question: Does the course include Generative Fill?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to direct Adobe Firefly Generative Fill inside Photoshop to add contextual background elements, replace objects, extend scene environments, and accelerate commercial compositing, while learning how to identify and manually fix AI-generated visual artifacts.

faq.question: Will I learn Harmonize and Generative Expand?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers Generative Expand for extending canvases seamlessly into new aspect ratios, and the Harmonize tool for matching foreground lighting, color temperature, and shadows to background environment plates, along with supported layer workflows and manual finishing techniques.

faq.question: Does the course require paid Adobe software?
faq.answer: Learners need access to Adobe Photoshop desktop (version 2024 or later recommended) via an active Adobe Creative Cloud subscription or trial. Nova Skills provides laboratory access during studio hours for classroom students. The curriculum teaches desktop Photoshop to ensure access to full professional production tools.

faq.question: Are AI generative credits included?
faq.answer: Adobe Creative Cloud plans include monthly generative credit allocations for Firefly features. The course is carefully structured to teach efficient, prompt-optimized workflows that do not require excessive credit usage, and manual Photoshop alternatives are taught for every AI-assisted step.

faq.question: Will I learn photorealistic compositing?
faq.answer: Yes. Commercial compositing is taught as a major discipline in Module 04. You will learn to evaluate and match camera focal length, perspective angles, horizon lines, lighting direction, color temperature, atmospheric falloff, and shadow physics to blend multiple photos into seamless, believable scenes.

faq.question: Does the course teach advertising design?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 05 focuses on commercial advertising creative production, teaching visual hooks, product hero positioning, message hierarchy, typography styling (headlines, body copy, CTA buttons), brand consistency, and high-converting e-commerce layouts.

faq.question: Will I learn 4:5, 1:1 and 9:16 campaign designs?
faq.answer: Yes. You will complete a dedicated multi-format campaign adaptation project creating 4:5 Portrait Feed (1080×1350 px), 1:1 Square Feed (1080×1080 px), and 9:16 Vertical Story/Reel (1080×1920 px) designs, mastering responsive composition without awkward stretching or cropping.

faq.question: Does the course include print-ready artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn prepress fundamentals including physical dimensions (mm/inches), effective PPI, CMYK color spaces, rich black vs pure black, ICC profile soft proofing, 3mm bleed, trim margins, and export to print-ready PDF/X formats.

faq.question: Will I receive editable PSD source files?
faq.answer: Yes, and more importantly, you will be trained to produce them. The course establishes strict PSD handover standards requiring 10 logical layer groups, non-destructive Smart Objects, and organized client delivery packages. A flattened JPEG alone does not qualify for course completion.

faq.question: What portfolio projects will I create?
faq.answer: You will build four major commercial portfolio projects: (1) Commercial Product Retouching Series across 3 varied products, (2) Photorealistic Commercial Composite, (3) Commercial Product Hero Advertisement, and (4) Three-Format Commercial Campaign Suite (4:5, 1:1, 9:16) with a complete client handover package.

faq.question: Does the course teach vector logo design?
faq.answer: No. Vector logo design and brand identity marks are the domain of vector illustration software (taught in our dedicated Adobe Illustrator course). Course 48 focuses strictly on raster image editing, photo retouching, compositing, and advertising creative production.

faq.question: Does it include advanced video editing or UI/UX?
faq.answer: No. Video editing and motion graphics are specialized in our Premiere Pro and After Effects courses, while digital product interface design is covered in our Figma UI/UX course. Course 48 strictly maintains focus on high-end commercial static imagery and advertising artwork.

faq.question: Is this an official Adobe certification?
faq.answer: This programme awards the Nova Skills Certified Commercial Photoshop Specialist (NS-CPS) credential, an independent institutional qualification certifying commercial production skills and verified portfolio execution. It is not an Adobe Certified Professional (ACP) exam voucher, though the curriculum thoroughly prepares students who wish to sit for ACP exams.

faq.question: What career opportunities are available?
faq.answer: Graduates are qualified for entry-level and junior commercial roles including Junior Photoshop Designer, Photo Retouching Assistant, Product Image Editor, E-commerce Image Editing Executive, Social Media Creative Designer, Advertising Creative Assistant, Digital Imaging Assistant, and Freelance Commercial Image Editor.

faq.question: What is Adobe Illustrator — Vector Graphics & Print Design?
faq.answer: Adobe Illustrator — Vector Graphics & Print Design is an intensive 6-week, 48-hour certification programme focused on precision vector drawing, Bézier curve mastery, professional typography, scalable icon systems, custom illustration, and commercial print prepress production. Students learn both traditional manual vector craftsmanship and cutting-edge Adobe Firefly AI vector tools, graduating with an industry-grade portfolio backed by fully editable .ai master source packages.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The programme starts with fundamental concepts in vector mechanics, interface navigation, geometric shape creation, and basic design principles before advancing systematically into advanced Pen Tool drawing, typography systems, vector illustration, and prepress engineering. No prior vector design experience is required.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is exactly 6 Weeks (48 total learning hours), priced at a transparent institutional fee of ₹6,900 (plus applicable 18% GST). Nova Skills follows a strict Truth in Pricing policy with zero artificial countdown discounts, inflated strike-through pricing, or hidden fees.

faq.question: Will I learn the Pen Tool and Curvature Tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Mastery over the Pen Tool and Curvature Tool is the central technical foundation of Module 02. You will learn to control Bézier handles, draft smooth curve tangents, place anchor points with mathematical efficiency, and construct clean vector paths with minimal anchor points.

faq.question: Does the course cover Pathfinder and Shape Builder?
faq.answer: Yes. Boolean shape operations are covered in depth. You will master both the Pathfinder panel (Unite, Minus Front, Intersect, Exclude, Divide, Trim, Merge) and the interactive Shape Builder Tool to rapidly combine, sculpt, and hollow out complex vector shapes.

faq.question: What is the difference between vector and raster graphics?
faq.answer: Raster graphics (like photos in Photoshop) are composed of a fixed grid of colored pixels that lose quality and become pixelated when enlarged. Vector graphics (in Illustrator) are built from mathematical paths, points, curves, and fills that scale infinitely to any size—from a 16px mobile icon to a 40-foot building billboard—with perfect razor-sharp clarity.

faq.question: Will I learn vector icon design?
faq.answer: Yes. Icon design is taught as a rigorous, systematic discipline in Modules 02 and 03. You will learn to construct icon grids, define stroke families, establish consistent corner radii, optically balance circular vs square masses, and export production-ready SVGs for mobile and web apps.

faq.question: How many icons will I create?
faq.answer: You will create a complete, cohesive family of exactly twelve vector icons. The project begins with a 6-icon precision construction lab in Module 02 and expands into a unified 12-icon design system accompanied by an icon specification sheet in Module 03.

faq.question: Does the course include professional typography?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 03 provides comprehensive training in commercial typography, covering typeface classifications, font pairing, character/paragraph formatting, optical kerning, proportional leading, Area Type vs Point Type, Type on Path, OpenType glyphs, and custom lettering foundations.

faq.question: Will I create an original illustration?
faq.answer: Yes. In Module 04, you will complete an original commercial vector hero illustration from thumbnail sketches to final digital artwork, applying advanced curve rendering, custom gradients, Gradient Mesh, the Blend Tool, and custom vector brushes.

faq.question: Will I learn Text to Vector Graphic?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to responsibly deploy Adobe Firefly Text to Vector Graphic inside Illustrator to explore concept variations, generate vector subjects and patterns via prompts, and integrate AI exploration into your creative process without sacrificing manual vector control.

faq.question: Does the course include Generative Shape Fill?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to use Generative Shape Fill to populate existing vector boundaries with contextually relevant, style-matched vector artwork, while learning how to direct color palettes and complexity levels.

faq.question: Can AI-generated vectors always be edited perfectly?
faq.answer: No, and understanding this limitation is a key learning outcome. Generative AI vectors frequently suffer from anchor point bloat, overlapping path artifacts, unwanted clipping masks, unclosed loops, and hidden raster elements. The course teaches rigorous manual inspection and geometry cleanup to bring AI assets up to commercial production standards.

faq.question: Will I learn print-ready PDF production?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 05 provides thorough prepress training, covering PDF/X standards, bleed settings, trim marks, printer marks, font embedding, transparency flattening, and preflight inspection in Adobe Acrobat to guarantee problem-free commercial printing.

faq.question: Does the course teach SVG export?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to configure clean SVG exports for digital products and websites, optimizing viewBox coordinates, eliminating unnecessary Illustrator metadata, and ensuring responsive scalability across modern web browsers.

faq.question: What are bleed and trim in print design?
faq.answer: Trim is the final physical cut line where the printed page is trimmed. Bleed is the extra area (typically 3mm or 0.125 inches) extending beyond the trim line where background colors and imagery are deliberately extended, preventing unsightly white paper borders when the guillotine cuts the paper stack.

faq.question: Will I receive editable Illustrator source files?
faq.answer: Yes, and you will be trained to produce and deliver them professionally. Every portfolio project requires native, editable .ai master working files organized across the 8 standard logical layer groups with live text preserved and non-destructive appearances intact.

faq.question: What portfolio projects are included?
faq.answer: You will build four major commercial portfolio projects: (1) Professional Vector Icon System (12-icon family), (2) Commercial Vector Illustration, (3) Editorial Typography Poster, and (4) Print & Digital Production Artwork (multi-artboard commercial campaign with full prepress packaging).

faq.question: Do I need an Adobe Illustrator subscription?
faq.answer: Learners need access to desktop Adobe Illustrator (version 2024 or later recommended) via an active Creative Cloud subscription or trial. Studio laboratory access is provided for classroom students during campus studio hours. Desktop Illustrator is required for full professional toolsets.

faq.question: Are Adobe generative credits included?
faq.answer: Adobe Creative Cloud plans include a monthly allocation of generative credits for Firefly features. The curriculum teaches efficient, prompt-optimized workflows that consume minimal credits, and manual vector drawing alternatives are provided for every AI-assisted technique.

faq.question: Does this course cover complete brand identity strategy?
faq.answer: No. Corporate brand positioning, extensive market research, and multi-touchpoint brand strategy are covered in separate specialized branding pathways. Course 49 focuses specifically on vector craft, icon design, typography, illustration, and commercial print production.

faq.question: Does the course teach professional vector logo research?
faq.answer: While you will learn foundational shape construction and typography essential for logo creation, specialized trademark legal clearance, comprehensive logo identity systems, and brand mark strategy belong to dedicated logo and brand identity courses.

faq.question: How is this course different from Adobe Photoshop?
faq.answer: Adobe Photoshop (Course 48) specializes in raster pixel editing, photo retouching, color grading, photorealistic compositing, and raster advertising banners. Adobe Illustrator (Course 49) specializes in mathematically scalable vector geometry, typography, icon systems, vector illustration, and print prepress.

faq.question: Is this an official Adobe certification?
faq.answer: This course awards the Nova Skills Certified Vector Graphics & Print Specialist (NS-VGPS) credential, an independent institutional qualification certifying practical commercial vector competency. It is not an Adobe Certified Professional (ACP) exam voucher, though the syllabus comprehensively prepares students wishing to sit for ACP exams.

faq.question: What career opportunities are available?
faq.answer: Graduates are qualified for entry-level and junior commercial design roles including Junior Vector Graphic Designer, Adobe Illustrator Designer, Vector Illustration Assistant, Icon Designer, Print Artwork Production Assistant, Advertising Artwork Assistant, Digital Asset Designer, and Freelance Vector Designer.

faq.question: What is Canva Professional — Brand & Marketing Design?
faq.answer: Canva Professional — Brand & Marketing Design is an intensive 4-week, 32-hour practical certification programme focused on visual hierarchy, typography, Brand Kits, original social media layouts, multi-slide carousels, 10-slide business presentations, reusable template systems, and responsible Canva AI workflows. Students learn to create marketing collateral starting from blank canvases rather than merely swapping text in premade templates, graduating with a commercial marketing toolkit backed by fully editable Canva source links.

faq.question: Is this Canva course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, this course is specifically structured for beginners including entrepreneurs, small business owners, educators, content creators, marketing assistants, and aspiring freelance designers. Training begins with foundational design principles—visual hierarchy, typography pairing, margins, spacing, alignment, and color harmony—ensuring learners develop solid graphic design fundamentals before creating complex marketing collateral.

faq.question: What is the course duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is 4 Weeks (32 guided learning hours), and the tuition fee is ₹4,900. Nova Skills maintains a transparent pricing policy with 0% fake discounts, no artificial comparison pricing, and no countdown timers.

faq.question: Do I need prior graphic design experience?
faq.answer: No prior graphic design experience or artistic training is required. You will learn the fundamental rules of visual communication, composition, and typography from the ground up, with step-by-step guidance from experienced design mentors.

faq.question: Will I learn Canva Brand Kits?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to build comprehensive Canva Brand Kits documenting exact HEX color swatches, primary and secondary font pairings, approved logo assets with clear-space rules, and structured folder organization. The course also teaches equivalent manual style workflows for learners utilizing free Canva accounts.

faq.question: Does the course teach typography and layout?
faq.answer: Yes, typography and layout are central pillars of the curriculum. You will master font pairing, scale hierarchy, leading, tracking, optical alignment, grid-based composition, and intentional whitespace to ensure every marketing design communicates clearly and looks professionally art-directed.

faq.question: Will I learn original social media design?
faq.answer: Yes. The course strictly emphasizes original layout craftsmanship. You will learn to construct social media creatives from blank canvases and custom grids, making intentional decisions about focal points, contrast, and balance rather than relying on overused, generic Canva templates.

faq.question: How many social designs will I create?
faq.answer: You will create eight original, standalone social media designs across multiple formats (1:1 square, 4:5 portrait, and 9:16 vertical), covering 8 distinct marketing objectives: product promo, service promo, educational post, event announcement, offer announcement, brand awareness, customer testimonial, and engagement prompt.

faq.question: Does the course include carousel design?
faq.answer: Yes. You will design a coherent, multi-slide educational or marketing carousel (5 to 7 slides) featuring an attention-grabbing first-slide hook, progressive visual storytelling, seamless slide-to-slide continuity, and a high-converting call-to-action slide.

faq.question: Will I learn Canva AI and Magic tools?
faq.answer: Yes. You will explore Canva's Magic Studio suite, including Magic Write, Magic Design, and Magic Media. Critically, you will learn rigorous human evaluation techniques to inspect generated layouts, correct typographic and alignment flaws, verify factual claims, and audit licensing compliance.

faq.question: Will I build reusable Canva templates?
faq.answer: Yes. You will construct a Reusable Canva Template Set containing at least four distinct layout patterns with component locking applied to key brand elements, allowing non-designers or clients to update text and photos without breaking the visual identity.

faq.question: Does the course teach business presentation design?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 4 is dedicated to business presentations. You will learn slide architecture, executive narrative pacing, clean typographic hierarchy, custom data visualizations, process workflows, and timeline diagrams in 16:9 widescreen format.

faq.question: How many slides will I create?
faq.answer: You will build a complete 10-slide executive business presentation deck covering cover, executive summary, problem, solution, benefits, workflow, custom data/comparison chart, proof, roadmap, and concluding call-to-action.

faq.question: Will I learn Canva collaboration?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn professional collaborative workflows including role-based permissions (Can View, Can Comment, Can Edit), inline feedback and comment resolution, version tracking, and safe sharing of master designs.

faq.question: Does the course cover Bulk Create?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn Bulk Create fundamentals—connecting external structured data from CSV files or Google Sheets to text variables and image placeholders to batch-produce multiple on-brand marketing variants safely.

faq.question: Will I learn content scheduling?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum introduces Canva's Content Planner, supported social media channel connections, and scheduling workflows, while emphasizing manual human review and approval gates before any live publication.

faq.question: Do I need Canva Pro?
faq.answer: No. All core learning outcomes and portfolio deliverables are fully achievable using a standard free Canva account alongside instructor demonstrations. Pro features are introduced where supported, but buying a paid subscription is never mandatory.

faq.question: Are Canva premium features included in the course fee?
faq.answer: No. The ₹4,900 tuition fee covers complete instructor-led training, practical laboratory exercises, individualized portfolio critique, and Nova Skills certification. Third-party Canva subscription fees are not bundled or falsely claimed as included.

faq.question: What is Figma UI Design & Responsive Prototyping?
faq.answer: Figma UI Design & Responsive Prototyping is an intensive 8-week, 64-hour practical specialization focused on interface design, Auto Layout mechanics, responsive web layouts, mobile app flows, component systems, design tokens, interactive prototyping, and developer handoff. Students learn to build interfaces that genuinely adapt across screen widths, graduating with a verified commercial UI portfolio backed by editable Figma source files.

faq.question: Is this Figma course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, this course is designed for beginners including aspiring UI designers, graphic designers entering digital product design, web designers, and frontend beginners. Training starts with fundamental UI principles—visual hierarchy, 8-point spacing grids, typography, and Figma workspace basics—before advancing to complex Auto Layout and component systems.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is 8 Weeks (64 guided learning hours across 6 modules), and the tuition fee is ₹9,900. Nova Skills maintains a transparent pricing policy with 0% fake discounts, no artificial comparison pricing, and no countdown timers.

faq.question: Do I need coding knowledge?
faq.answer: No programming or coding knowledge is required. All core coursework, Auto Layout exercises, component design, and prototyping are executed visually within Figma Design and FigJam. However, the course teaches developer handoff principles so you understand how your designs translate cleanly into HTML, CSS, and frontend frameworks.

faq.question: Will I learn website and mobile app UI design?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum covers both responsive web interfaces (desktop, tablet, and mobile web layouts) and native mobile application screen flows (incorporating mobile touch targets, navigation patterns, and app states).

faq.question: What is Auto Layout in Figma?
faq.answer: Auto Layout is Figma's powerful layout engine that mimics modern CSS flexbox and grid behavior. It allows frames and components to grow, shrink, wrap, and reorder automatically based on content and container dimensions, forming the foundation of modern responsive interface design.

faq.question: Will I learn Hug, Fill and Fixed sizing?
faq.answer: Yes, mastering Hug Contents, Fill Container, and Fixed dimensions is a core technical milestone. You will learn exactly when and how to apply each sizing constraint, along with min/max width and height bounds, to ensure nested elements behave predictably during viewport resizing.

faq.question: Will I learn responsive website design?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to construct responsive website structures that reflow gracefully across screen sizes, adapting multi-column product grids, card layouts, content sections, and navigation systems without horizontal overflow or broken elements.

faq.question: Can Figma layouts resize when frame width changes?
faq.answer: Yes. Using Figma Design's Auto Layout, constraints, Fill Container settings, and min/max dimensions, frames and nested components dynamically expand, contract, and wrap as the parent frame width is resized manually.

faq.question: Can a desktop menu automatically become a hamburger menu?
faq.answer: In standard Figma Design, continuous frame dragging does not automatically swap component variants between desktop links and a mobile hamburger icon; that structural breakpoint change is accomplished using configured component variants, documented breakpoint frames, or interactive prototypes. The course clearly teaches the distinction between continuous responsive reflow and structural variant switching.

faq.question: What is the difference between Figma Design responsiveness and Figma Sites breakpoints?
faq.answer: Figma Design uses Auto Layout and constraints for fluid resizing within frames, while structural breakpoint changes require explicit variant configurations. Figma Sites (where available) supports defined CSS-style breakpoints that automatically switch responsive component variants at specific viewport thresholds. The course teaches both concepts accurately.

faq.question: Will I learn responsive product cards and grids?
faq.answer: Yes. You will complete dedicated hands-on labs engineering responsive product cards with dynamic text wrapping, fixed image aspect ratios, and multi-column product grids that reflow smoothly across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.

faq.question: Will I learn Figma components and variants?
faq.answer: Yes. You will master main components, instances, component sets, and variants across multiple interaction states (default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled), along with component properties such as boolean toggles, text fields, and instance swap slots.

faq.question: Does the course cover design tokens and variables?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to set up Figma variables for colors, numbers, and strings, organizing them into collections and distinguishing primitive tokens (raw values) from semantic tokens (functional design roles like background-primary or text-secondary).

faq.question: Will I learn light/dark mode design?
faq.answer: Yes. You will build a dual-theme UI system using Figma variable modes, demonstrating how an entire multi-screen interface instantly switches between Light and Dark themes through semantic token mapping.

faq.question: Will I create interactive prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 5 is dedicated to interactive prototyping. You will connect multi-screen flows, configure click/hover triggers, implement modal and drawer overlays, and animate state transitions using Smart Animate.

faq.question: How many mobile app screens will I design?
faq.answer: You will design a complete, cohesive mobile app user journey comprising at least five high-fidelity screens: Home feed, Search/Browse with filters, Product Detail, Cart/Saved Items, and Checkout Confirmation.

faq.question: Will I create a responsive e-commerce website?
faq.answer: Yes. Portfolio Project 01 requires building a fully responsive commercial e-commerce website featuring Homepage, Product Listing Page (PLP), and Product Detail Page (PDP) tested across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.

faq.question: What is Figma Dev Mode?
faq.answer: Figma Dev Mode is a dedicated workspace for developers to inspect design measurements, copy CSS and token values, view component properties, compare versions, and download production-ready assets. The course covers Dev Mode workflows alongside manual handoff methods.

faq.question: Will I learn developer handoff?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to prepare professional developer handoff specifications, including organized frame naming, layout and spacing annotations, CSS token documentation, exportable SVG assets, and design QA checklists.

faq.question: Does the course cover Figma Make and Figma Sites?
faq.answer: Yes, Figma Make (for AI-assisted prototype exploration) and Figma Sites (for breakpoint-based web layout demonstrations) are introduced as supporting capabilities where accessible, while keeping core manual UI craftsmanship in Figma Design as the primary focus.

faq.question: Do I need a paid Figma plan?
faq.answer: No. All core learning outcomes, Auto Layout exercises, component systems, and portfolio deliverables are fully achievable using a standard free Figma account alongside instructor demonstrations of advanced features.

faq.question: What portfolio projects will I build?
faq.answer: You will complete four primary portfolio deliverables: (1) Responsive E-commerce Website UI (Homepage, PLP, PDP), (2) Five-Screen Mobile App Flow, (3) Reusable UI Component Library with Design Tokens & Light/Dark Modes, and (4) Clickable Prototype & Developer Handoff Package.

faq.question: Is this a complete UX research programme?
faq.answer: No. Course 51 is a focused UI production and responsive prototyping specialization. While it covers screen architecture, wireframes, and basic user flows, comprehensive UX research methodologies, user interviews, and product strategy belong to the extended UI/UX Design Professional programme.

faq.question: What is the difference between this course and UI/UX Design Professional?
faq.answer: Course 51 focuses deeply on hands-on UI execution in Figma—Auto Layout, responsive screens, design tokens, component variants, prototypes, and developer handoff (8 weeks, 64 hours). UI/UX Design Professional is a longer, broader qualification covering extensive UX research, usability testing, and product strategy.

faq.question: Is this an official Figma certification?
faq.answer: No. This is an industry-recognized professional certification issued by Nova Skills Education Institute validating practical Figma UI design and responsive prototyping craftsmanship. It is not an official corporate certification from Figma Inc.

faq.question: What entry-level career opportunities can I explore?
faq.answer: Graduates can explore entry-level opportunities such as Junior UI Designer, Figma UI Designer, Responsive Web Designer, Mobile App UI Assistant, UI Component Designer, and Developer Handoff Design Assistant.

faq.question: What is Brand Identity Design & Visual Systems?
faq.answer: Brand Identity Design & Visual Systems is an intensive 8-week, 64-hour applied specialization focused on developing complete, research-informed visual identity systems for commercial businesses. Students learn client discovery, creative direction, logo families, typography, color calibration, supporting graphic devices, multi-touchpoint brand applications, and comprehensive brand guidelines, graduating with two complete assessed brand case studies.

faq.question: Is this an advanced or beginner course?
faq.answer: This is an Applied Specialization requiring foundational vector-design knowledge. It is not an introductory software tool course. Learners should already understand basic Illustrator tools (shapes, Pen Tool, basic typography) so instruction can focus on strategic thinking, creative direction, systems design, and client-level brand delivery.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is 8 Weeks (64 guided learning hours across 6 modules), and the tuition fee is ₹10,900. Nova Skills maintains a transparent pricing policy with 0% fake discounts, no artificial comparison pricing, and no countdown timers.

faq.question: Do I need prior Illustrator knowledge?
faq.answer: Yes, basic vector design knowledge in Adobe Illustrator is required. Students should be comfortable creating documents, manipulating vector paths, using the Pathfinder tool, and handling type and color palettes before enrolling.

faq.question: Is there a vector-design readiness assessment?
faq.answer: Yes, students can complete an Illustrator readiness checklist confirming basic competence in shapes, path editing, alignment, layer organization, and vector file export before beginning the course.

faq.question: What is the difference between a logo and brand identity?
faq.answer: A logo is simply a primary identifying mark or signature. A visual brand identity is an entire sensory ecosystem comprising logo configurations, typography hierarchies, color proportions, graphic devices, imagery art direction, and compositional rules that ensure a brand is instantly recognizable even without its logo present.

faq.question: Will I learn brand research?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 1 is dedicated to brand discovery, client questionnaires, stakeholder interviews, audience profiling, and translating business objectives into concrete visual design criteria.

faq.question: Does the course cover competitor analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to perform competitor visual identity audits, mapping category visual conventions, color and typography trends, and positioning white-space to identify genuine differentiation opportunities.

faq.question: Will I learn creative direction?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 2 teaches you how to bridge strategy and visual aesthetics, establishing distinct conceptual visual territories, curating targeted moodboards, and formulating written creative rationales.

faq.question: What is a visual territory?
faq.answer: A visual territory is an explored conceptual direction that embodies a specific brand personality through a unified combination of typography, color palette, photographic mood, and graphic language before finalizing logo designs.

faq.question: Will I learn complete logo systems?
faq.answer: Yes. You will design cohesive logo families including primary lockups, secondary stacked or horizontal layouts, compact symbols, monochrome versions, and reversed treatments calibrated for diverse backgrounds and scales.

faq.question: Does the course cover typography and color systems?
faq.answer: Yes. You will establish rigorous typography hierarchies (display, heading, body, caption) with leading and tracking rules, alongside calibrated color systems specifying exact HEX, RGB, CMYK, and spot color swatches.

faq.question: Will I create brand patterns and graphic elements?
faq.answer: Yes. Every brand identity system requires at least two custom supporting graphic devices, such as bespoke brand patterns, proprietary vector framing shapes, or custom icon styles that enrich brand touchpoints.

faq.question: Does the course include photography direction?
faq.answer: Yes. You will develop photography art direction guidelines specifying lighting style, subject composition, color grading, and treatment rules to ensure all future brand imagery aligns with the visual identity.

faq.question: Will I design stationery and digital brand assets?
faq.answer: Yes. You will apply the identity system across at least five purposeful touchpoints, including stationery (business cards, letterhead, email signatures), digital marketing assets (social templates, web hero banners), and environmental collateral.

faq.question: What is a brand-guidelines document?
faq.answer: A brand-guidelines document (often 12–20 pages) is an authoritative manual that documents logo usage, exclusion zones, minimum sizes, approved color breakdowns, typography scales, graphic rules, application examples, and prohibited misuses.

faq.question: Will I learn how to prepare editable brand assets?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn professional asset packaging: organizing layers in Illustrator, creating global swatches, outlining type for production, exporting web-ready SVGs and PNGs, and structuring an 8-folder client handover archive.

faq.question: Which software will I use?
faq.answer: The primary tools are Adobe Illustrator (for vector marks, systems, and guidelines) and Adobe Photoshop (for photography treatments and realistic mockups). Figma is used for digital touchpoints, and Adobe Acrobat for PDF guideline QA.

faq.question: How many brand identity projects will I complete?
faq.answer: You will complete two distinct, comprehensive commercial case studies: (1) a complete visual identity system for a new business, and (2) a strategic brand identity refresh and repositioning for an existing enterprise.

faq.question: Will both case studies include guidelines?
faq.answer: Yes. Both case studies must include a full brand-guidelines document, five or more purposeful applications, and an organized 8-folder client handover archive.

faq.question: Is this course different from Course 54 Logo Design?
faq.answer: Yes. Course 52 focuses on complete visual identity systems, creative direction, multi-touchpoint applications, and brand guidelines. Course 54 is a dedicated deep-dive into standalone logo craftsmanship, geometric mark construction, and specialized symbol design.

faq.question: Does the course provide legal trademark clearance?
faq.answer: No. The course teaches visual differentiation and preliminary risk awareness, but formal trademark searches, legal clearance, and registration require qualified intellectual property legal professionals.

faq.question: Does the course include full UI/UX design?
faq.answer: No. While digital brand touchpoints (such as website hero sections and social assets) are designed in Figma, comprehensive UI/UX prototyping and research are covered in Course 51 (Figma UI Design) and UI/UX Design Professional.

faq.question: Are Adobe software subscriptions included?
faq.answer: No. The ₹10,900 course fee covers complete instructor-led training, project reviews, curriculum access, and certification. Adobe Creative Cloud subscriptions must be acquired separately by students.

faq.question: Is this an official Adobe certification?
faq.answer: No. This is an industry-recognized professional credential issued by Nova Skills Education Institute validating your practical visual identity design and systems craftsmanship. It is not an Adobe-issued certification.

faq.question: What freelance services can I offer?
faq.answer: Graduates can offer premium freelance services including comprehensive brand identity packages, brand identity refreshes, logo family systems, professional brand guidelines manuals, and marketing collateral design kits.

faq.question: What entry-level career opportunities are possible?
faq.answer: Graduates can explore opportunities such as Junior Brand Identity Designer, Visual Identity Designer, Creative Design Associate, Brand Collateral Designer, Junior Art Direction Assistant, and Marketing Brand Designer.
