main_topics: 1. Microsoft Teams Workspace & Channels: Architecture of Teams and Channels (General vs Private); chat formatting (rich text, announcements); mentions (`@team`, `@name`); sharing and co-authoring files within tabs; managing notifications and availability status (Available, Busy, Do Not Disturb).

2. Online Meeting Preparation & Facilitation: Structuring concise meeting agendas; setting meeting options (lobby controls, presenter roles, mic/camera permissions); meeting invitation distribution; screen sharing etiquette (window vs full screen); recording consent and privacy etiquette; capturing live notes.

3. Formal Minutes of Meeting (MoM) Drafting: The architecture of professional meeting minutes: Meeting Metadata (date, time, attendees, absentees), Agenda Overview, Discussion Summaries, Formal Decisions Taken, Action Item Matrix (Task, Owner, Due Date, Deliverable), and Next Meeting Schedule.

4. Operational Task Management: Microsoft To Do task management; organizing daily tasks with 'My Day'; setting deadlines, reminders, and recurring tasks; introduction to Microsoft Planner for team Kanban boards; assigning task ownership, priority levels (Urgent, Important, Medium), and tracking completion.

5. Digital Form Design & Data Collection: Designing intake forms using Microsoft Forms or Google Forms; structuring question types (text, multiple-choice, rating, date, file upload); setting required fields and input validation; configuring form settings (who can respond, accept responses deadline); testing form usability.

6. Form Data Processing & Privacy Governance: Distributing form links and QR codes; monitoring real-time responses; exporting raw response tables directly into Excel; auditing response data hygiene; anonymizing sensitive survey data; data privacy standards under organizational rules.

7. End-to-End Office Workflow Coordination: Step-by-step administrative coordination lifecycle: receiving executive requests, breaking requests into assigned tasks, scheduling synchronization meetings, authoring and circulating minutes, tracking task completion, and issuing executive status reports.
detailed_subtopics: Professional Communication in Teams: Differentiating between channel posts (transparent, team-wide communication) and private chats (confidential 1:1 coordination); formatting announcements with header banners; professional emoji and reaction etiquette in corporate workspaces; managing notification overload.

Digital Meeting Logistics & Etiquette: Meeting preparation checklist: testing audio/microphone 10 minutes prior, staging presentation files, configuring the Teams meeting lobby to admit external guests securely, muting noisy participants, managing the chat stream, and closing meetings promptly on schedule.

Minutes of Meeting (MoM) Engineering: Translating 45 minutes of unstructured verbal discussion into a crisp 1-page executive document; avoiding conversational transcripts; focusing exclusively on key deliberations, agreed resolutions, and accountability matrices; distributing minutes within 24 hours of meeting completion.

Task Triage & Execution Tracking: Structuring personal and team workflows in Microsoft To Do: synchronizing flagged Outlook emails into To Do tasks; creating dedicated lists (`Apex Operations`, `Vendor Deliveries`, `Audit Prep`); setting hard due dates and escalating overdue tasks.

Form Architecture & Question Validation: Designing clean office intake forms (e.g. Employee Training Feedback or Office Supplies Requisition); utilizing dropdowns to prevent typos; enforcing mandatory response fields; formulating clear instructions; evaluating response summaries via automated charts.

Integrated Coordination Lifecycle: Executing a simulated operational event: an office relocation coordination project requiring an initial briefing meeting, published staff requirement survey, compiled minutes of meeting, and 5 assigned operational follow-up tasks.

learning_objectives: Understand capabilities and limitations of generative AI in office operations: text drafting, cognitive acceleration, formula troubleshooting, and summarization vs hallucinations and factual errors.
Formulate structured office prompts using the 7-part framework: Task, Context, Audience, Output Format, Tone, Constraints, and Review Instructions.

Condense lengthy reports, meeting transcripts, and email threads into concise, actionable executive briefings using AI assistance.
Execute rigorous human-in-the-loop verification: cross-checking numbers, verifying dates/names, catching hallucinations, and correcting unjustified claims.

main_topics: 1. Generative AI in the Modern Digital Workplace: Understanding Large Language Models; capabilities of Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Google Gemini; cognitive acceleration vs unverified automation; recognizing fundamental AI limitations (lack of real-time ground truth, statistical guessing).

2. Structured Prompt Engineering for Office Tasks: The 7-part enterprise prompting framework: (1) Core Task, (2) Organizational Context, (3) Target Audience, (4) Output Format & Structure, (5) Professional Tone, (6) Negative Constraints (what to avoid), and (7) Review Instructions.

3. AI-Assisted Document Drafting & Editing: Drafting formal business letters, operational notices, executive summaries, meeting agendas, and policy memos; rewriting text for clarity, conciseness, and formality; proofreading for subtle grammatical inconsistencies.

4. AI for Spreadsheets & Formula Troubleshooting: Asking AI to explain complex nested formulas (`=INDEX/MATCH` vs `=XLOOKUP`); troubleshooting `#VALUE!` and `#N/A` errors; generating formula recommendations; mandatory rule: every formula suggested by AI must be independently tested and calculated.

5. AI-Assisted Presentation Development: Generating presentation outline concepts; condensing 10-page reports into 8 bulleted slide summaries; refining bullet points for visual clarity; fact-checking numerical data against source spreadsheets.

6. AI for Email & Meeting Management: Drafting polite follow-up messages; converting rough notes into structured email responses; summarizing 20-message email chains; extracting action items and assigned deadlines; verifying recap completeness.

7. The Human-in-the-Loop Imperative & Verification Protocols: Verification checklist: checking every calculation, confirming person names and dates, detecting plausible hallucinations, catching invented facts or policies, approving final deliverables, and maintaining independent manual software mastery.

8. AI Security, Privacy & Organizational Guardrails: Enterprise data privacy rules; prohibiting input of customer Personally Identifiable Information (PII), passwords, financial ledgers, or trade secrets into public AI tools; understanding organizational licensing; ethical and responsible AI usage standards.
detailed_subtopics: The 7-Part Prompting Architecture: Deconstructing weak prompts ('Write an email about the meeting') into professional prompts ('Act as an executive assistant for Apex Solutions. Draft a formal follow-up email to the Department Heads summarizing the decisions of today's budget meeting. Audience: Senior Leadership. Tone: Respectful, professional, action-oriented. Format: 3 bulleted decisions followed by an Action Items table. Constraints: Do not exceed 250 words; do not invent budget figures; leave placeholder brackets for specific amounts.'); analyzing output quality.

Formula Verification & Mathematical Integrity: Using AI to explain complex formulas; testing AI-generated formula suggestions against real Excel data; discovering where AI provides deprecated syntax or hallucinates non-existent function arguments; verifying calculations with manual mental math and control totals.

Summarization & Cognitive Extraction: Feeding a 4-page unformatted operational report into an AI assistant; prompting it to extract: (1) Executive Summary, (2) Top 3 Operational Risks, and (3) Required Next Steps; comparing AI summary against the full source document to detect omitted critical nuances or hallucinated claims.

Hallucination Detection & Red Teaming Exercise: Inspecting 3 deliberately flawed AI responses containing subtle factual errors (wrong tax percentages, fictitious labor laws, inverted date chronologies); documenting the errors; rewriting the content to 100% accuracy.

Enterprise Data Privacy Standards: Prohibited data categories for public AI prompts: Credit card details, Aadhaar/PAN/National ID numbers, unreleased quarterly financial numbers, employee medical records, customer phone numbers; practicing data sanitization (replacing real names with 'Client A' and amounts with '₹[Amount]').

Independent Competence Guarantee: Reinforcing the core educational principle: AI is a junior drafting assistant, never an authoritative decision-maker. The student remains personally accountable for every word, formula, and number submitted.

main_topics: 1. Capstone Scenario Architecture & Enterprise Brief: Role, responsibilities, and operational scope of an Office Administrator for 'Apex Enterprise Solutions' (a 50-person growing professional services enterprise); reviewing administrative pain points and setting up the master project repository.

2. Capstone Component A — Professional Corporate Documentation: Creating the standardized corporate document pack: formal letterhead memorandum, official office policy notice, structured meeting agenda, executive Minutes of Meeting (MoM), 6-page operational report with automated Table of Contents and section breaks, and standardized document templates.

3. Capstone Component B — Spreadsheet Operations & Reporting Engine: Building the master operational Excel workbook: 30-day employee attendance register with automated counts, departmental petty cash and expense ledger with absolute tax formulas, customer sales and order register featuring XLOOKUP and in-cell data validation, inventory supplies tracker with automated reorder flags, dynamic PivotTable summaries with date grouping, and 3 executive business charts.

4. Capstone Component C — Executive Business Presentation: Designing an 8–10 slide corporate review deck in Microsoft PowerPoint: custom Slide Master branding, corporate color palettes, typography pairings, live-linked Excel operational charts, visual card layouts, purposeful transitions, and comprehensive speaker notes on every slide.

5. Capstone Component D — Email Communication & Calendar Scheduling: Developing the executive communications dossier in Microsoft Outlook: professional meeting invitations, client inquiry responses, vendor payment follow-up letters, escalation notices, conflict-free executive calendar schedule, recurring team sync configuration, and email security phishing triage documentation.

6. Capstone Component E — Cloud Collaboration & Access Governance: Setting up collaborative cloud operations in Google Workspace and Microsoft OneDrive: shared project proposal with Suggesting mode edits and resolved comments, live operational tracking sheet, documented least-privilege permission architecture (Viewer/Commenter/Editor), restricted link sharing, and version history restore proof.

7. Capstone Component F — Governed AI Productivity Dossier: Documenting at least two applied AI office workflows: prompt engineering logs using the 7-part framework, raw AI-generated drafts, human-in-the-loop redline audits, detected error/hallucination corrections, and finalized verified deliverables.

8. Capstone Component G — Final Demonstration, Live Defense & Oral Evaluation: Conducting a live 10-minute executive presentation: showing the completed toolkit, explaining core spreadsheet formulas, defending management report observations, demonstrating cloud sharing, identifying and independently correcting an intentionally introduced software error, and fielding instructor Q&A.
detailed_subtopics: Master Toolkit Compilation & Organization: Creating the standardized digital submission directory structure: `Apex_Admin_Toolkit_[StudentName]/` containing 6 categorized subfolders (`01_Documentation`, `02_Spreadsheets`, `03_Presentations`, `04_Communications`, `05_Cloud_Collaboration`, `06_AI_Verification`); verifying file naming conventions (ISO-8601 dates, version tags) across all 15 evidence deliverables.

Cross-Tool Document Consistency: Ensuring corporate brand harmony across Word documents, PowerPoint slides, and Excel workbooks: consistent primary font pairing, matching company logo placements, identical corporate hex color codes, and unified header/footer styling.

Spreadsheet Quality & Control Total Auditing: Conducting pre-submission formula audits on the master operational workbook: confirming zero `#N/A`, `#VALUE!`, or `#DIV/0!` errors; validating that all summary cards tie back to raw transactions with zero variance; ensuring data validation dropdowns prevent data corruption; verifying print setups.

The 7-Step Capstone Demonstration Protocol: (1) Walk through the master folder directory, (2) Present the 6-page Word corporate report and explain section break logic, (3) Demonstrate the Excel workbook, explaining XLOOKUP and PivotTable slicers, (4) Present 3 slides from the executive deck in Presenter View, (5) Walk through the Google Workspace shared document and version history, (6) Locate and fix an intentionally injected error (e.g. broken VLOOKUP or corrupt validation rule) live without notes, and (7) Explain AI prompt engineering logs and verification safeguards.

Technical Defense & Q&A Strategy: Preparing for instructor questions on: formula efficiency, why specific chart types were chosen over others, how cloud permissions prevent data breaches, and how AI hallucinations were detected and mitigated.

Final Dossier Packaging & Institutional Archival: Compiling working editable files (`.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`), cloud link documentation, and a single master PDF executive dossier for permanent institutional grading and verifiable digital portfolio publication.

business_data_accuracy_framework.heading: Accurate Excel Reports Begin With Accurate Data
business_data_accuracy_framework.reconciliationRule: Raw Source Total → Formula Summary → PivotTable Total → Management Report. Numbers must reconcile across all layers.
exceptionHandling: Inspect cell data types (numbers stored as text).
Identify missing records and broken lookups.

modern_excel_function_compatibility.targetSoftware: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365 (Windows Desktop preferred)
modern_excel_function_compatibility.versionPolicy: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365 is the primary classroom software. Newer perpetual versions (Excel 2021/2024) support XLOOKUP and dynamic arrays, whereas older versions like Excel 2016 and 2019 do not natively support XLOOKUP or dynamic arrays.
modern_excel_function_compatibility.fallbackTeaching: For older Excel installations, students learn legacy lookup patterns (INDEX/MATCH and exact-match VLOOKUP) while understanding why modern functions are standard in current office environments.
modern_excel_function_compatibility.dynamicArraySpillRule: Dynamic arrays return multiple values across adjacent worksheet cells. Spill areas must be unblocked. Spilled array formulas cannot live as normal calculated columns inside Excel Tables; tables serve as data sources and standard worksheet ranges receive spilled outputs.

excel_tables_vs_pivottables.excelTable: A structured relational data container supporting column headers, instant filtering, structured references, automatic row expansion, and self-inheriting calculated columns.
excel_tables_vs_pivottables.pivotTable: An analytical calculation engine that summarizes, groups, and cross-tabulates records across rows, columns, filters, and value aggregations.
excel_tables_vs_pivottables.refreshRule: Updating source data in an Excel Table does not automatically refresh connected PivotTables. Students must execute a manual or workbook refresh to recalculate report figures.

csv_hygiene_policy.heading: CSV Hygiene & File Safety
commonRisks: Leading zeros stripped from numeric IDs, ZIP codes, and phone numbers.
Date formats misinterpreted between MM/DD and DD/MM locales.
Currency symbols causing numeric columns to convert to uncalculable text.
Formula injection risk: external CSV cells beginning with '=', '+', '-', or '@' executing code when opened directly in spreadsheets.
csv_hygiene_policy.safePractice: Inspect data in import preview windows, explicitly set column data types to Text for IDs before importing, and utilize Power Query or the Text Import Wizard rather than blindly double-clicking external CSV files.

curriculum.title: Excel Foundations & Data Quality
curriculum.objective: Develop correct foundational habits for working with business spreadsheets and structured data.
lessons: 1.1 Introduction to Microsoft Excel: Spreadsheet purpose.; Office workflows.; Business reporting.; Common practical applications.
1.2 Excel Interface: Ribbon.; Formula bar.; Name box.; Worksheets.; Workbook navigation.; Quick Access Toolbar awareness.
1.3 Workbook Fundamentals: Create.; Open.; Save.; Save As.; File formats.; Worksheet naming.
1.4 Cells and Ranges: Row.; Column.; Cell address.; Range.; Selection.
1.5 Data Entry: Text.; Numeric data.; Dates.; Percentages.; Currency.; Blank cells.
1.6 Data Types: Number vs text.; Dates as serial values.; Text-based IDs.; Common errors.
1.7 Cell References: Relative references.; Absolute references.; Mixed references.; Fill behaviour.
1.8 Basic Calculation: Arithmetic operators.; Order of operations.; Basic formula syntax.
1.9 Essential Formatting: Number formats.; Currency.; Percentages.; Dates.; Decimal precision.
1.10 Professional Formatting: Alignment.; Readable headings.; Consistent fonts.; Borders.; Table formatting.; Controlled colours.
1.11 Excel Tables: Insert Table.; Headers.; Table names.; Auto-expanding table rows.; Calculated columns.
1.12 Structured Business Data: One record per row.; One variable per column.; Unique column headings.; No merged cells in source tables.; No blank separator rows.
1.13 Sorting: Single-column sorting.; Multi-column sorting.; Avoiding partial-range sorting errors.
1.14 Filtering: AutoFilter.; Date filters.; Numeric filters.; Text filters.; Clear filters.
1.15 Data Quality: Missing values.; Duplicate records.; Wrong data types.; Inconsistent spelling.; Invalid dates.
1.16 Error Prevention: Correct headings.; Unique identifiers.; Consistent data entry.; Input documentation.; Source preservation.
1.17 Freeze Panes: Maintaining header visibility.; Navigation.
1.18 Basic Worksheet Protection Awareness: Preventing accidental formula changes.; Protection is not a substitute for information security.
1.19 File Organization: Version naming.; Source files.; Reporting files.; Backups.
1.20 Basic Troubleshooting: #### display.; Number stored as text.; Incorrect dates.; Broken references.; Formula entered as text.

curriculum.title: Business Formulas & Functions
curriculum.objective: Apply essential Excel formulas to realistic business reporting problems and independently verify the results.
lessons: 2.1 Formula Fundamentals: Equals sign.; Operators.; Arguments.; Function structure.; Parentheses.
2.2 References in Formulas: Relative.; Absolute.; Mixed.; Copying formulas.
2.3 Basic Functions: SUM.; AVERAGE.; MIN.; MAX.; COUNT.; COUNTA.; Teach as building blocks, not the entire assessment focus.
2.4 SUMIF vs SUMIFS: Conditional sums.; Multiple criteria.; Dates.; Product categories.; Salespersons.
2.5 COUNTIF vs COUNTIFS: Counting records.; Attendance.; Status reports.; Multiple conditions.
2.6 IF: Logical tests.; Business rules.; Status labels.; Eligibility conditions.
2.7 IFS: Multiple conditions.; Ordered tests.; Default cases.; Appropriate use.
2.8 AND / OR: Combined conditions.; Validity checks.; Eligibility rules.
2.9 IFERROR: Handling expected error cases.; Clear messages.; Formula quality.; Important: Do not teach IFERROR as a method of hiding all errors without investigation.
2.10 Lookup Concepts: Unique identifiers.; Lookup tables.; Exact matches.; Missing values.
2.11 XLOOKUP: Lookup value.; Lookup array.; Return array.; Exact match.; Not-found handling.
2.12 XLOOKUP Business Examples: Product price lookup.; Employee department lookup.; Inventory category lookup.; Commission category lookup.

faq.question: What is Microsoft Excel — Business Reporting & Data Analysis?
faq.answer: It is a practical Excel certification covering formulas, structured data, data validation, PivotTables, charts and business reporting.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Six weeks, with 48 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹6,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified fee and tax policy.

faq.question: Is the course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It begins with Excel fundamentals.

faq.question: Do I need prior Excel knowledge?
faq.answer: No. Basic computer and arithmetic skills are sufficient.

faq.question: Which Excel version is used?
faq.answer: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365, preferably the Windows desktop version.

faq.question: Will I learn Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, including SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IF, IFS, IFERROR and XLOOKUP.

faq.question: Will I learn XLOOKUP?
faq.answer: Yes. XLOOKUP is part of the mandatory curriculum.

faq.question: Will I learn VLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH?
faq.answer: Students receive useful awareness of legacy lookup methods, while XLOOKUP is the main modern lookup function.

faq.question: What are dynamic arrays?
faq.answer: They are modern Excel formulas capable of returning results across multiple worksheet cells.

faq.question: Will I learn FILTER, UNIQUE and SORT?
faq.answer: Yes. These are included in the modern Excel module.

faq.question: Why do some formulas not work in older Excel versions?
faq.answer: Modern functions depend on the Excel version. Older installations may lack XLOOKUP or dynamic-array functionality.

faq.question: Will I learn data validation?
faq.answer: Yes, including suitable restrictions and drop-down lists.

faq.question: Will I learn conditional formatting?
faq.answer: Yes, for useful tasks such as highlighting exceptions and business statuses.

faq.question: Will I learn PivotTables?
faq.answer: Yes. PivotTables are a major part of the course.

faq.question: Will I learn charts and reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. Students practise charts, PivotCharts, KPIs and business summaries.

faq.question: Will I learn dashboards?
faq.answer: The course teaches practical reporting summaries with charts and PivotTables, not complex enterprise BI dashboards.

faq.question: Will I learn Power Query?
faq.answer: Yes, at an introductory level for importing and preparing data.

faq.question: Will I learn Power BI?
faq.answer: No. Power BI belongs to an advanced MIS/Business Intelligence pathway.

faq.question: Will I learn VBA or macros?
faq.answer: No. VBA automation is outside this certification.

faq.question: Will I learn Python in Excel?
faq.answer: No. The course concentrates on Excel foundations and applied reporting.

faq.question: Is Copilot required?
faq.answer: No. Copilot is optional and depends on licensing and feature availability.

faq.question: Can AI help with Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, but students must understand and independently verify all formula outputs.

faq.question: What business reports will I create?
faq.answer: A sales tracker, an expense or attendance report and a final Excel reporting workbook.

faq.question: What will my final capstone include?
faq.answer: Structured data, validation, formulas, a PivotTable, charts, quality checks and a management summary.

faq.question: Will I learn CSV import?
faq.answer: Yes, including data types, encoding, dates and common import issues.

faq.question: Will I learn to identify spreadsheet errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Formula errors, invalid data and report reconciliation are important parts of the course.

faq.question: Is this suitable for office executives?
faq.answer: Yes. The content focuses on common office reporting and data analysis work.

faq.question: Can small business owners take this course?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers practical sales, expense and inventory reporting applications.

faq.question: What can I study next?
faq.answer: Suitable progression may include advanced Excel, Business Productivity Mastery and longer MIS/Business Intelligence programs. ---

styles_accessibility_framework.heading: Create Documents That Are Structured, Not Just Visually Formatted

directFormattingVsStyles.directFormatting: Applying bold, enlarged font sizes, or color highlights directly to individual paragraphs creates visual emphasis but lacks semantic meaning or navigation support.
directFormattingVsStyles.headingStyles: Applying Heading 1, Heading 2, and Heading 3 styles establishes a logical document hierarchy, powers the Navigation Pane, enables one-click automatic tables of contents, and ensures assistive technology accessibility.

accessibilityPrinciples: Logical heading hierarchy (no skipped heading levels without reason)
Accessible tables with designated repeating header rows and no complex merged cells
Descriptive hyperlink text (avoiding ambiguous 'click here' labels)
Informative alternative text (alt text) for meaningful images, with decorative images flagged
High visual contrast and readable font sizing
Clean structural PDF export preserving heading tags and reading order
styles_accessibility_framework.accessibilityCheckerGuide: Located on the Review tab, the Accessibility Checker scans for missing alt text, unlabelled table headers, contrast issues, and structural defects. Human judgment remains essential to confirm reading flow, clarity, and logical sense.

mail_merge_technical_guide.heading: Personalize Multiple Documents Without Manually Replacing Every Name
mail_merge_technical_guide.coreArchitecture: Mail merge connects a main Word document with a structured recipient dataset (Excel), populates dynamic merge fields, and compiles personalized outputs.
excelDataHygiene: Row 1 must contain clean, unique column headers.
Each subsequent row must represent exactly one recipient.
Postal codes and identification codes must be formatted explicitly as Text to prevent Excel from stripping leading zeros.
Date columns must use standardized date formats.
No blank rows, sub-headers, or merged cells in the source table.
commonPitfalls: Leading zeros lost in postal codes or phone numbers.
Connecting to the wrong worksheet in a multi-tab workbook.
Missing merge fields causing blank gaps in letter salutations.
Currency values losing formatting during field merge.
Paragraph formatting shifting when recipient names vary in length.
mail_merge_technical_guide.privacyAndScope: Mail merge is practiced with fictional classroom datasets. The course does not require bulk marketing campaigns, live email transmissions, or external mailing APIs.

desktop_vs_web_policy.desktopVsWebDistinction: While Microsoft Word for the web provides convenient cloud editing and real-time co-authoring, advanced features—including full Excel-to-Word mail merge, legal document comparison, advanced section break handling, content controls, and rich Accessibility Checker options—require the full desktop client.
desktop_vs_web_policy.classroomDemonstrations: Desktop installations are used for feature demonstrations. Students using browser-based Word are provided with guided desktop recordings and laboratory walkthroughs.

scope: Saving DOCX files directly to cloud storage for versioning
Sharing documents with specific people or teams

Real-time co-authoring awareness and version history restoration
Revoking or adjusting access permissions upon review completion
onedrive_collaboration_policy.privacyNotice: No personal paid OneDrive subscription is required. Cloud exercises are conducted with institutional or fictional practice files without accessing personal user accounts.

protectionAwareness: Read-only mode and 'Mark as Final' signal document completion but do not provide cryptographic security.
Restrict Editing limits formatting changes or forces Track Changes for reviewers.
Password protection adds file encryption for opening or modifying.
Important limitation: Document restrictions and read-only flags can often be bypassed; they do not replace secure data handling.
finalDocumentQAChecklist: 1. Document Title, recipient name, and reference numbers verified.
2. Correct current dates and company contact details.
3. Consistent font families, sizes, and paragraph spacings throughout.
4. Page setup, margins, and page orientations verified.
5. Headers, footers, and page numbers correctly configured.
6. Automatic Table of Contents refreshed with updated page numbers.
7. All captions and table/figure numbers checked.
8. Table borders, cell alignments, and header rows audited.
9. Hyperlinks tested for accurate destination URLs.
10. All comments and tracked revisions resolved and accepted/rejected.
11. Document Inspector run to remove unwanted metadata or hidden personal information.
12. Accessibility Checker passed without unresolved structural errors.
13. Tagged PDF export verified for visual fidelity, text selection, and reading flow.

pdf_delivery_guide.heading: Deliver a Document That Remains Readable Outside Microsoft Word
accessiblePdfStandards: Exporting directly via File > Export > Create PDF/XPS (or Save As PDF) with document structure tags enabled.
Preserving heading bookmark hierarchies for instant navigation in PDF readers.
Ensuring text remains selectable (not converted to flattened raster images).
Retaining clickable hyperlinks and accessible table headers.
pdf_delivery_guide.verificationProtocol: Open the exported PDF in a standard PDF viewer, check page count, confirm margins and table borders match the Word source, verify that text can be highlighted and copied, and ensure no confidential draft notes remain.

mandatoryHumanVerification: Verify all names, dates, financial sums, and factual figures independently.
Ensure AI-generated content does not introduce fabricated company policies or contractual commitments.
AI cannot replace Word formatting skills: students must manually construct styles, manage section breaks, execute mail merge, and configure accessibility.
Never upload private HR records, customer databases, or proprietary corporate data to unapproved public AI tools.

portfolio.title: Professional Document Production Portfolio
portfolio.objective: Demonstrate practical, job-relevant Microsoft Word capability through four verified office deliverables: a structured business report, a reusable corporate template/letterhead, an Excel-based bulk mail merge, and a tracked-changes document review, supported by accessible PDF exports and quality assurance checklists.
portfolio.countingRule: Four core required deliverables: 1. Structured Business Report, 2. Business Letterhead & Reusable Template, 3. Bulk Personalized Letters (Mail Merge), and 4. Tracked-Changes Professional Review, accompanied by PDF delivery files and a document QA checklist.

deliverables.title: Structured Business Report
deliverables.scenario: Prepare a professional departmental monthly performance or office operations report for management review.
mandatory_content: Cover page with document title, organization, date, author/department, and version
Executive overview and structured body sections
Data-presenting business tables with repeating header rows
Key operational findings and actionable recommendations
mandatory_word_features: Section and page break management (no repeated empty Enter presses)
Headers and footers with automated page numbering
qa_checks: Verify all section headings reflect correctly in the Navigation Pane.
Update the entire table of contents to ensure accurate pagination.
Confirm no accidental blank pages exist.
Verify table readability and cell alignment.
Inspect exported PDF against original DOCX layout.

deliverables.title: Business Letterhead & Reusable Template
deliverables.scenario: Design an editable, standardized corporate letterhead and correspondence template for a small business or department.
required_elements: Organization branding and header identity
Contact section and standardized margins
Consistent typography and paragraph rules
Date and reference number placeholders

deliverables.title: Excel-to-Word Mail Merge Letters
deliverables.scenario: Generate personalized business notification or training invitation letters from a structured Excel recipient dataset using fictional records.
mandatory_process: 1. Prepare and validate a clean synthetic Excel spreadsheet with first-row column headers.
2. Ensure postal codes and numeric IDs are stored as Text to preserve leading zeros.
3. Connect the Word main letter document to the Excel data source via the Mailings tab.
4. Insert address blocks, personalized greeting lines, and dynamic merge fields.
5. Preview merged records, inspecting first, middle, last, and long-text records.
6. Complete the merge to generate individual personalized documents without VBA.
7. Review representative outputs for formatting alignment and missing fields.
deliverables.privacy_rule: Use strictly fictional or anonymized recipient information. No real personal contact data collection or live bulk email sending is required.

deliverables.title: Tracked-Changes Professional Review
deliverables.scenario: Conduct a structured document review of a departmental report draft, simulating a professional editing and approval workflow.
required_process: 1. Open the original report draft and activate Track Changes.
2. Make suggested textual corrections, rewordings, and formatting enhancements.
3. Insert constructive review comments and query unresolved points.
4. Utilize Compare Documents to inspect differences between draft versions.
5. Systematically accept or reject revisions based on editorial standards.
6. Run Word's Accessibility Checker to detect and rectify structural issues.
7. Prepare a clean, approved final version with all revisions resolved and comments cleared.
8. Export the approved document to an accessible distribution-ready PDF.
deliverables.critical_rule: Disabling Track Changes does not accept or remove existing revisions. A clean final document requires explicit acceptance or rejection of all recorded edits.

assessment_model.criticalAssessmentPrinciple: A document must be structurally correct, accessible, and functional—not merely visually decorated. Proper heading styles, automatic table of contents, and clean mail merge mapping are mandatory passing requirements.

slide_master_policy.heading: Design Once. Reuse Consistently.
slide_master_policy.coreArchitecture: Slide Master view governs master-level branding, typography inheritance, and custom layout placeholders across the entire presentation.
slide_master_policy.desktopVsWebRequirement: Full authoring and editing of custom Slide Master layouts requires the desktop edition of Microsoft PowerPoint. PowerPoint for the web supports applying existing layouts but does not provide complete custom Slide Master authoring.
commonErrors: Pasting logos manually across individual slides instead of placing on the Slide Master.
Hardcoding text box dimensions on slide bodies instead of using master placeholders.
Inconsistent margins caused by manual drag-and-drop alignment.
Font incompatibilities when non-standard fonts are used without embedding.

chart_linking_policy.heading: Keep the Information Editable—and the Numbers Accurate.

methods.nativePowerPoint: Insert Chart directly within PowerPoint, storing data in an embedded mini-worksheet. Preferred for portable, standalone decks.
methods.embeddedExcel: Copy an existing Excel chart and embed the workbook within PowerPoint. Fully editable, but caution required to prevent accidental sharing of confidential source sheets.
methods.linkedExcel: Link PowerPoint directly to an external Excel file for real-time data updates. Requires maintaining exact relative file paths; broken links occur if the source workbook is moved, renamed, or delivered without dependencies.
methods.staticImage: Pasting as a picture is reserved for fixed historical references only; core business presentations must use editable charts.

chart_linking_policy.handoverRule: When delivering presentations to clients, test all chart links and confirm whether embedded standalone data or external linked workbooks are required.

information_design_ethics.heading: A Good Chart Must Be Accurate Before It Is Attractive.
qualityChecks: Zero baseline maintained for bar and column charts to prevent visual scale exaggeration.
Explicit measurement units, currency symbols, and reporting timeframes clearly stated.
No misleading 3D effects that distort data slice perspectives.
Meaningful contrast and non-colour-only data encoding for accessibility.
Documented data source footnotes on every analytical slide.

motion_accessibility_policy.heading: Use Motion to Explain—not Distract.
principles: Transitions should be subtle and restrained (Fade or Push) with consistent duration (0.5s–0.8s).
Morph transitions provide smooth object transformation across duplicate slides where supported by Microsoft 365 or modern perpetual editions.
Animation Pane must be used to sequence complex reveals progressively, preventing cognitive overload.
Motion must never trigger photosensitive discomfort or distract from core business comprehension.
accessibilityChecklist: Unique and descriptive slide titles on every slide for screen reader navigation.
Verified reading order configured in the Selection Pane or Reading Order Pane.
High-contrast text against solid or subtle backgrounds (minimum 4.5:1 ratio).
Informative alternative text (alt text) for photos and diagrams, flagging decorative elements.
Pass PowerPoint's built-in Accessibility Checker without unresolved structural warnings.

supportingTools: Microsoft Excel (for chart data modeling and linked workbooks)
Canva or Adobe Photoshop (for supplementary image editing and graphic asset preparation)
Microsoft Copilot in PowerPoint (optional, where licensed, for drafting slide outlines and summaries)
tools_policy.responsibleAiRule: AI-generated slide drafts must undergo rigorous human verification: verify all numbers, eliminate fabricated factual claims, and convert generic layout outputs into custom Slide Master designs.

curriculum.practical_assignment: Create a reusable corporate PowerPoint template.
curriculum.assessment:
A reusable PowerPoint template such as `.potx`, plus a reviewable `.pptx` demonstration where appropriate.

A `.thmx` theme may be supplied as supporting evidence.

### IMPORTANT TECHNICAL DISTINCTION

A PowerPoint theme and a PowerPoint template are related but not identical.

A theme primarily specifies coordinated colours, fonts and effects.

A template can include the theme plus master layouts, placeholders and reusable structure.

Creating and saving a custom template requires suitable desktop PowerPoint functionality.

Do not claim that PowerPoint for the web provides identical Slide Master authoring capabilities.

A PowerPoint theme and a PowerPoint template are related but not identical.

portfolio.title: Professional Presentation Design Portfolio
portfolio.objective: Develop and verify three distinct presentation design deliverables: a complete 12-slide corporate business deck, a reusable Slide Master theme/template system, and a 5-slide before/after redesign exercise, supported by editable source files and export quality checklists.
portfolio.countingRule: Three separate deliverables: 1. A 12-slide business deck, 2. A reusable PowerPoint template system (.potx/.pptx), and 3. A 5-slide before/after presentation redesign exercise.

deliverables.title: Corporate Business Presentation (12-Slide Deck)
deliverables.scenario: Create a complete, cohesive 12-slide corporate presentation based on a realistic business brief covering company overview, market problem, core solutions, process workflows, KPI results, editable chart analysis, implementation roadmap, and strategic recommendations.
suggested_slide_structure: Slide 1: Corporate Cover (Brand identity, title, subtitle, presenter metadata)
Slide 2: Executive Overview (High-level summary and meeting objectives)
Slide 3: Business Context / Problem Statement (Market challenge and pain points)
Slide 4: Target Audience / Market Landscape (Demographics and opportunity)
Slide 5: Core Product / Service Solution (Value propositions and features)
Slide 6: Process / Workflow Diagram (Visual step-by-step methodology)
Slide 7: Operational Data / KPI Summary (Card metrics and reporting period)
Slide 8: Editable Business Chart Analysis (Native PowerPoint column/bar chart)
Slide 9: Strategic Comparison Matrix (Alternatives and competitive advantages)
Slide 10: Implementation Plan / Project Timeline (Phased milestone roadmap)
Slide 11: Key Recommendations & Financial Impact (Evidence-based takeaways)
Slide 12: Closing Summary / Call to Action (Next steps and contact details)
mandatory_skills: Strict visual hierarchy and editorial headline structures
Consistent brand styling (typography pairings, palette harmony, grid layout)
Editable native PowerPoint charts (no full-slide static screenshots)
Process diagrams and infographics built with PowerPoint shapes
Slide Master layout inheritance and non-overflowing text boxes
Accessibility check and high-resolution PDF export

deliverables.title: Corporate PowerPoint Theme & Template System
deliverables.scenario: Design an institutional presentation design system built directly inside Slide Master to ensure company-wide formatting consistency.
required_components: Theme colour palette with defined primary, accent, and background tones
Theme font definitions (coordinated header and body typefaces)
Slide Master with master-level header, footer, and slide number controls
At least 5 custom slide layouts: 1. Cover, 2. Section Divider, 3. Text & Image, 4. Chart/KPI, 5. Summary/Closing
Standardized content, text, and media placeholders positioned on a consistent grid
Brief template usage instructions documenting font rules and placeholder behavior

deliverables.title: Five-Slide Before/After Presentation Redesign
deliverables.scenario: Diagnose and resolve five critical presentation design problems across five distinct poorly formatted source slides.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Poor Typography to Clear Editorial Hierarchy
redesign_cases.original_problem: Excessive font sizes, weak contrast, and unreadable wall of body text.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Strong action headline, consistent 2-level typographic hierarchy, and intentional line-spacing.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Cluttered Layout to Clean Focused Composition
redesign_cases.original_problem: Decorative clip-art icons, unnecessary shapes, and zero whitespace creating cognitive overload.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Simplified 3-column layout with ample whitespace, aligned elements, and purposeful iconography.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Misleading Chart to Honest Data Visualization
redesign_cases.original_problem: Distorted 3D pie chart with truncated axes, missing units, and unlabelled categories.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Clean 2D horizontal bar chart with zero baseline, clear data labels, source note, and key takeaway.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Inconsistent Branding to Harmonious Brand System
redesign_cases.original_problem: Mismatched random colors, conflicting fonts, and misaligned text boxes.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Applied corporate theme colors, standardized fonts, and snapped elements to a 12-column grid.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Dense Text Wall to Structured Process Infographic
redesign_cases.original_problem: Lengthy multi-paragraph description of an operational workflow.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Converted narrative into an editable 4-step horizontal process diagram with concise summary captions.

deliverables.deliverable_format: 10-slide comparative presentation (5 original problem slides + 5 redesigned solution slides) with concise design rationale notes.

assessment_model.completionRule: Students must submit the complete 12-slide business deck, reusable template system, and 5-slide before/after redesign exercise with editable source files. Visual decoration without underlying master-layout discipline or editable chart accuracy will not receive passing evaluation.

faq.question: What is Microsoft PowerPoint — Professional Presentation Design?
faq.answer: It is a practical PowerPoint certification focused on professional slide design, templates, editable charts, accessible presentations and business-ready file delivery.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Four weeks with 32 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the fee?
faq.answer: ₹4,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic computer knowledge is sufficient.

faq.question: What software will I learn?
faq.answer: Microsoft PowerPoint is the primary software.

faq.question: Will I learn visual design principles?

cloud_security_and_permissions_policy.heading: Collaborate Without Accidentally Sharing Sensitive Information
principles: Least-Privilege Access: Grant Viewer or Commenter access by default; reserve Editor for active co-authors.
Permission Inheritance: Understand that child files inherit folder access; broadly shared folders cannot be partially locked down from within.
Restricted Confidential Folders: Keep sensitive financial, HR, or client records in dedicated restricted locations rather than general team drives.
Owner Privacy: Recognize that sharing links and files exposes the owner's account identity to viewers; use supervised test environments in training.
Version History Auditing: Track collaborator revisions, inspect timestamps, and restore earlier clean drafts when unwanted modifications occur.

forms_and_linked_sheets_policy.heading: Collect Information Once. Organize It Responsibly.
principles: Independent Permission Audits: Google Forms collaborators do not automatically share the same access rules as the linked response Sheet; both must be audited independently.
Synthetic Classroom Datasets: Real client PII, government IDs, student personal details, or financial accounts must never be collected or stored in practice forms.
Data Minimization: Request only the fields strictly required for the business process; use validation rules to ensure data integrity.
Downstream Refresh Awareness: Linked Sheets accept new submissions automatically, but downstream reports, pivot summaries, and dashboard slides require deliberate configuration or manual refresh.

responsible_gemini_ai_policy.heading: Use Gemini to Assist Work. Keep Humans Responsible for Decisions.
principles: AI as Assistant: Use Gemini for drafting emails, outlining slide decks, summarizing reports, and explaining formulas, never as the unverified source of truth.
Mandatory Factual Verification: Cross-check every date, stakeholder name, numeric calculation, and contractual deadline against verified source documents.
Free-Account Fallback: Certification exercises never require a paid Gemini tier; instructors provide synthetic AI sample outputs for manual review where accounts lack AI licenses.
Data Confidentiality: Prohibit pasting non-public enterprise information or client details into public or consumer AI prompts.

meeting_and_communication_standards.heading: Professional Connected Communication Standard
principles: Asynchronous Precision: Write structured emails with explicit subjects, numbered action items, clear assignees, and stated deadlines.
Timezone Diligence: Verify multi-region attendees in Google Calendar before issuing invitations; configure working hours and buffer times.
Meet Professional Etiquette: Arrive with prepared Docs agendas, designate a scribe for follow-up documentation, and establish explicit consent before initiating any recorded session.
Paid Feature Transparency: Acknowledge that recording, automated transcription, and AI meeting summaries are tier-dependent and not universal across free accounts.

tools_and_licensing_boundary.heading: Core Accessible Tools vs. Paid Workspace Features
principles: Core Tools Covered: All foundational skills utilize Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Meet, and Forms available across personal and standard Google accounts.
No Admin Console Requirement: Enterprise domain provisioning, DNS record mapping, Google Vault, and DLP rules are excluded from this operational certification.
Shared Drives Awareness: Organization-managed shared storage is taught conceptually; individual lab work operates safely within My Drive hierarchies.
Introductory Apps Script: Script triggers and macros are presented as awareness concepts; no JavaScript or Apps Script programming is required to earn certification.

curriculum.title: Cloud Workplace & Security
curriculum.objective: Understand Google Workspace fundamentals, organize cloud information and use appropriate file-access and security practices.
lessons: 1.1 Cloud Productivity Fundamentals: Cloud applications; Browser-based work; File synchronization; Team collaboration; Connected workflows.
1.2 Consumer Google vs Google Workspace: Personal Google account; Organization-managed Workspace account; Account ownership; Subscription differences; Administrative policies.
1.3 Workspace Application Ecosystem: Gmail; Drive; Docs; Sheets; Slides; Calendar; Meet; Forms; Tasks; Gemini awareness.
1.4 Google Account Security: Password practices; Two-step verification; Account recovery awareness; Device security; Phishing prevention.
1.5 Google Drive Navigation: My Drive; Files; Folders; Search; Starred; Shortcuts; Recent files interface.
1.6 Folder Architecture: Project folders; Department folders; Shared resources; Archive systems; Naming conventions.
1.7 File Organization: Document naming; Version designations; Date conventions; Ownership structure; Folder purpose definition.
1.8 File Uploads & Conversions: Uploading local files; Office-to-Docs conversion where appropriate; File preview; Direct opening; Safe download protocols.
1.9 Google File Types: Native Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms; Handling uploaded Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files.
1.10 Sharing Fundamentals: Restricted access; Adding specific people; General link sharing; Recognizing primary file ownership.
1.11 Permission Roles: Viewer permissions; Commenter permissions; Editor permissions; Owner roles and delegation.
1.12 Least-Privilege Access: Granting minimum necessary permissions; Avoiding widespread editor access; Periodic external sharing audits.
1.13 Inherited Permissions: Folder-level sharing dynamics; Child file access inheritance; Effective permissions; Limits on restricting a file inside a broadly shared folder.
1.14 Restricted Folders: Isolating sensitive departmental materials; Limiting subfolder visibility where supported; Preventing confidential leaks.
1.15 Shared Drives Awareness: Organization-managed shared drives; Team-owned storage vs personal My Drive; Subscription and admin requirements.
1.16 File Ownership Management: Creator vs owner; Collaborator rights; Ownership transfer protocols and organizational restrictions.
1.17 Version History & Recovery: Tracking revisions; Identifying collaborator edits; Restoring earlier clean versions; Creating named milestone versions.
1.18 File Recovery & Trash Governance: Google Drive Trash lifecycle; Restoring deleted files; Recovery limitations; Ownership deletion impact.
1.19 Offline Access Awareness: Enabling Google Docs offline mode; System setup requirements; Synchronization risks on shared devices; Data safety.
1.20 Security Risks & Best Practices: Mitigating public link leaks; Preventing accidental external editors; Avoiding unnecessary downloads; Protecting sensitive spreadsheets.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Create an office folder structure using fictional business information featuring main workspace, project, documents, reports, meetings, forms, and deliverables folders. Demonstrate restricted files, viewer, commenter, editor access, version history, and a permissions audit.
curriculum.deliverable: Google Drive Office Workspace & Permission Matrix
curriculum.security_considerations: Use only synthetic business information. Never make all files public for convenience; enforce strict least-privilege role assignment.

curriculum.title: Gmail, Calendar & Meet
curriculum.objective: Manage professional email, scheduling, meetings and follow-up workflows efficiently and accurately.
lessons: 2.1 Gmail Professional Communication: Inbox organization; Compose; Reply; Reply All discipline; Forwarding; Business signatures.
2.2 Professional Email Structure: Clear subject lines; Professional greetings; Structured body copy; Explicit call-to-action; Standard sign-offs.
2.3 Recipient Management: Appropriate use of To, CC, and BCC; Preserving client privacy; Avoiding accidental company-wide replies.
2.4 Attachments & Drive Sharing: Direct attachments vs Google Drive links; Automatic permission verification before sending; File-size limits.
2.5 Gmail Labels: Creating hierarchical labels; Color-coding projects; Differentiating internal vs client conversations.
2.6 Gmail Filters & Automation: Automating inbox triage based on sender, subject, and keywords; Applying labels; Archiving and skipping inbox.
2.7 Advanced Gmail Search: Search operators (from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment, filename:, after:, before:); Finding lost communications.
2.8 Stars, Priority & Snooze: Multi-star systems for triage; Snoozing emails for future review; Zero-inbox workflow principles.
2.9 Email Templates: Creating and inserting reusable email drafts; Interface and account requirements for template activation.
2.10 Business Email Quality Assurance: Verifying email objectives; Proofreading recipient addresses; Checking attached links; Professional tone.
2.11 Calendar Fundamentals: Navigating Day, Week, Month, and Schedule views; Creating and categorizing personal and team events.
2.12 Event Scheduling Discipline: Informative event titles; Descriptive meeting briefs; Timezone validation; Setting appropriate notification buffers.
2.13 Calendar Invitations & RSVP: Inviting internal and external guests; Tracking RSVP statuses (Yes, Maybe, No); Managing updates and cancellations.
2.14 Multi-Timezone Coordination: Managing time differences across India and global zones; Secondary timezone display; Preventing scheduling conflicts.
2.15 Recurring Meetings & Exceptions: Setting up daily standups, weekly reviews, and monthly townhalls; Modifying single occurrences vs series.
2.16 Shared Calendars Awareness: Viewing team availability; Creating secondary departmental calendars; Calendar visibility settings.
2.17 Google Meet Fundamentals: Joining sessions via link, Calendar, or phone; Microphone and camera settings; Meeting chat; Screen sharing controls.
2.18 Meeting Roles & Controls: Meeting organizer; Host management tools; Co-host delegation where supported; Participant management and muting.
2.19 Meeting Agendas in Practice: Drafting clear objectives, discussion topics, time allocations, and expected decision outcomes in Docs.
2.20 Virtual Meeting Etiquette: Punctuality, background audio hygiene, camera conventions, screen presentation protocols, and consent standards.
2.21 Meeting Follow-Up Documentation: Capturing decisions, assigning action items with explicit owners and deadlines, and compiling follow-up notes.
2.22 Meet Recording Awareness: Workspace plan eligibility; Host permissions; Recording storage in Drive; Mandatory participant notification and consent.
2.23 Meeting Transcription & AI Notes: Plan requirements for automated transcriptions; Supported language limits; AI summary review and correction.
2.24 Integrated Communication Workflow: Connecting email invitations, Calendar events, Meet links, shared Docs agendas, and Sheets tracking.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Prepare a complete fictional team meeting workflow: draft an invitation email, schedule a Calendar event with Meet details, prepare an agenda in Docs, allocate action items, write a follow-up email, and record decisions in a tracker.
curriculum.security_considerations: Perform labs using supervised practice accounts; never send unsolicited invitations to external third parties; respect meeting consent guidelines.

curriculum.title: Docs, Sheets & Slides
curriculum.objective: Create and maintain professional collaborative documents, spreadsheets and presentations.
lessons: 3.1 Connected Office Documents: Interoperability between text, data, and slides; Shared cloud file ownership; Universal version tracking.
3.2 Google Docs Interface: Modern Docs navigation; Document outline; Page setup; Word count; Full-screen and pageless views.
3.3 Professional Document Structure: Title hierarchy; Headings (H1, H2, H3); Body typography; Bulleted lists; Tables; Visual breaks.
3.4 Styles & Formatting Consistency: Applying and updating default styles; Document styling templates; Enhancing readability and scanability.
3.5 Real-Time Docs Collaboration: Co-authoring etiquette; Commenting (@mentioning team members); Suggesting mode; Accepting and rejecting edits.
3.6 Document Version History: Reviewing historical revisions; Naming significant milestone versions; Comparing edits across collaborators.
3.7 Document Sharing Protocols: Managing Viewer, Commenter, and Editor access; Preventing unauthorized download, copy, or print on sensitive files.
3.8 Smart Chips in Docs: Embedding interactive chips for people, files, dates, calendar events, and dropdown status trackers.
3.9 Google Sheets Fundamentals: Grid architecture; Rows, columns, cells, and ranges; Data formats (numbers, currency, dates, text).
3.10 Business Formulas in Practice: Essential office formulas (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, COUNTA, COUNTIF, SUMIF, basic IF logic, and TODAY).
3.11 Team Task & Operations Tracker: Designing structured trackers with Task ID, Description, Assignee, Priority, Status, Due Date, and Notes.
3.12 Data Validation Controls: Configuring dropdown menus for status fields; Preventing invalid text entries; Enforcing clean team inputs.
3.13 Conditional Formatting: Highlighting overdue deadlines; Flagging high-priority issues; Visualizing project completion percentages.
3.14 Sorting, Filters & Filter Views: Quick sorting; Multi-column filtering; Creating collaborative Filter Views without altering teammates' views.
3.15 Basic Spreadsheet Reporting: Summary calculation cards; Category counts; Status distribution charts; Clear labeling and headers.
3.16 Collaborative Editing in Sheets: Concurrent editing rules; Cell commenting; Protecting specific ranges and sheets to avoid accidental overwrites.
3.17 Google Slides Fundamentals: Setting up presentation decks; Applying theme masters; Working with layouts, text boxes, and shapes.
3.18 Shared Presentations: Multi-user deck collaboration; Slide-level commenting; Assigning slide review tasks; Presentation approvals.
3.19 Business Slide Design Quality: Contrast and typography standards; Avoiding crowded text; Creating structured 3-part layout cards.
3.20 Linking Spreadsheet Information: Importing charts and tables from Sheets into Slides; Linked vs unlinked insertion modes.
3.21 Linked-Data Limitations: Understanding update and refresh mechanics; Handling broken links; Permission requirements for linked source sheets.
3.22 Cloud Version Control: Reconciling divergent versions; Archiving old presentations; Ensuring single source of truth across team assets.
3.23 Exporting & File Conversion: Exporting Docs to PDF; Exporting Sheets to CSV/PDF; Converting Slides to PPTX/PDF; Preserving fidelity.
3.24 Document Accessibility Fundamentals: Using true headings for screen readers; Providing alternative text for images; Ensuring WCAG contrast.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Build a collaborative team project package: 1 professional Google Doc with styles and comments, 1 Google Sheets tracker with data validation and formulas, 1 Google Slides update presentation with linked chart, and version history evidence.
curriculum.deliverable: Google Docs + Sheets + Slides Team Collaboration Pack
curriculum.security_considerations: Maintain strict boundary: does not replace advanced Excel data modeling or Word desktop publishing. Use clean, non-confidential operational data.

curriculum.title: Forms & Team Workflows
curriculum.objective: Use Forms, Sheets, Drive and appropriate task-coordination practices to manage recurring office workflows.
lessons: 4.1 Digital Office Workflow Concepts: Inputs, validation, processing, team review, reporting outputs, and clear process ownership.
4.2 Google Forms Fundamentals: Form creation; Title, description, sections; Header branding; Organizing question flow logically.
4.3 Question Types & Validation: Short answer, paragraph, multiple choice, checkboxes, dropdown, linear scale, date, and input validation rules.
4.4 Form Design & UX: Writing unambiguous questions; Grouping related items into sections; Avoiding unnecessary data collection.
4.5 Required Fields & Branching: Setting mandatory fields; Section navigation based on user answers; Ensuring clean submission pathways.
4.6 Form Settings Management: Email collection controls; Limiting to 1 response; Enabling response editing; Confirmation messages.
4.7 Form Access & Permissions: Collaborator editing access vs respondent submission access; Differentiating editor rights from respondent rights.
4.8 Publishing & Controlled Distribution: Generating short URLs; Embedding in internal docs; Restricted organizational sharing vs public access.
4.9 Analyzing Form Responses: Viewing aggregate summaries, question breakdowns, and individual response submissions in Google Forms.
4.10 Linking Forms to Google Sheets: Creating a new response spreadsheet; Linking to an existing destination sheet; Managing incoming timestamps.
4.11 Response Sheet Permissions Governance: Independent security: why removing a Form collaborator does NOT revoke access to the linked Sheet.
4.12 Data Quality & Sanitization: Handling duplicate submissions; Standardizing text inputs; Validating date formatting in the response sheet.
4.13 Workflow Case 1 — Internal Service Request: Request submission via Form; Automatic row logging; Triage assignment; Status tracking in Sheets.
4.14 Workflow Case 2 — Office Feedback Survey: Anonymous feedback collection; Aggregating satisfaction metrics; Presenting chart summaries in Slides.
4.15 Google Tasks Coordination: Creating personal and shared task lists; Assigning due dates; Integrating Tasks within Gmail and Google Calendar.
4.16 Team Operations Coordination: Establishing task owners, priorities, progress milestones, and scheduled weekly review checkpoints.
4.17 Drive Folder Architecture for Workflows: Organizing form drafts, raw response datasets, cleaned reporting sheets, and executive presentations.
4.18 Access Governance Auditing: Restricting access to raw survey response data; Applying principle of least privilege across operational pipelines.
4.19 Shared Drives in Team Workflows: Understanding organizational file ownership; Member permissions (Manager, Content Manager, Contributor, Viewer).
4.20 Version Control for Operational Workflows: Documenting changes to form questions; Managing revision notes in response trackers.
4.21 Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Documentation: Writing clear step-by-step documentation for form management, data review, and handoff.
4.22 Human Approval & Sign-Offs: Structuring human checkpoints in office workflows; Avoiding claims of unverified total automation.
4.23 Google Apps Script Awareness: Architectural overview of Apps Script; Concept of triggers (onEdit, onFormSubmit); Security permissions and risks.
4.24 Privacy, Compliance & Data Ethics: Minimizing personal data collection; Storing consent records; Establishing retention and deletion schedules.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Design and deploy an internal-office request workflow: create a Google Form, collect synthetic submissions, route data to a linked Google Sheet, build an operational tracking view with validation and status tags, and audit permissions.
curriculum.security_considerations: Crucial rule: Verify both Form and linked Sheet permissions independently. Never collect real PII, financial details, or government IDs in classroom forms.

curriculum.title: Gemini-Assisted Productivity
curriculum.objective: Understand how eligible Gemini features can assist everyday office tasks while maintaining human accountability, accuracy and data privacy.
lessons: 5.1 Gemini Ecosystem Overview: Gemini standalone app vs embedded Gemini features across Google Workspace applications; Feature boundaries.
5.2 Plan Eligibility & Subscriptions: Free Google accounts vs Google Workspace Business/Enterprise tiers vs Google AI Pro add-ons.
5.3 Free vs Paid Feature Availability: Identifying which AI features are included by plan; Understanding feature rollouts and administrative toggles.
5.4 Gemini in Gmail: Drafting professional emails; Summarizing long email threads; Adjusting tone (formal, concise, elaborate); Human review.
5.5 Gemini in Google Docs: 'Help me write' drafting; Rewriting text for clarity; Summarizing documents; Structuring executive summaries.
5.6 Gemini in Google Sheets: Generating formula suggestions; Explaining complex formula logic; Organizing data categories; Creating starter tables.
5.7 Gemini in Google Slides: Brainstorming presentation outlines; Drafting slide headlines and bullet points; Generating concept imagery.
5.8 Advanced Slides Generation Awareness: Multi-slide generation updates (June 2026); Plan eligibility (Business Standard+, Google AI Pro); Language limits.
5.9 Gemini in Google Drive: Summarizing stored documents and reports; Finding information across authorized files without manual reading.
5.10 Gemini in Google Meet: Automated meeting notes (where licensed); Action item extraction; Consent protocols and participant notification.
5.11 Gemini in Google Forms: Assisted form and survey generation; Drafting relevant question options; Human review of question bias.
5.12 Business Prompting Framework: Structuring prompts with Task, Context, Source Data, Constraints, Desired Output Format, and Verification.
5.13 AI for Business Correspondence: Drafting meeting requests, follow-up notes, vendor responses, and executive announcements safely.
5.14 AI for Document Editing: Checking draft completeness; Formatting unstructured notes into clean tables; Refining tone for external audiences.
5.15 AI for Spreadsheet Interpretation: Deciphering unfamiliar formulas; Verifying mathematical assumptions; Checking calculation boundaries manually.
5.16 AI for Presentation Planning: Generating structured 5-slide deck structures from written briefs; Outlining key takeaways and speaker points.
5.17 Understanding AI Hallucinations: Recognizing invented facts, incorrect dates, fabricated meeting decisions, and erroneous spreadsheet formulas.
5.18 Rigorous Factual Verification: Cross-referencing AI outputs against primary records; Validating figures, names, deadlines, and direct quotes.
5.19 Human Accountability & Approval: The mandatory rule of human sign-off: never sending AI drafts without line-by-line editorial inspection.
5.20 Enterprise Data Privacy & Security: Rules against inputting confidential client records, employee personal data, or proprietary trade secrets.
5.21 Responsible AI Workflow Standard: The 6-step cycle: Draft → Review → Verify → Correct → Approve → Deliver.
5.22 Free-Account Classroom Fallback: Using instructor-provided synthetic AI outputs for evaluation exercises when student accounts lack AI tiers.
5.23 AI as Copilot, Not Replacement: Demonstrating manual proficiency across all core Google apps before applying AI acceleration.
5.24 Feature Rollout & Policy Monitoring: Monitoring Google Workspace updates, regional availability, language support, and institutional controls.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Perform three supervised AI assistance exercises using synthetic data: improve an email draft, summarize an office report, and explain a formula/outline. Identify and correct deliberate AI hallucinations. Use provided sample outputs if Gemini is unavailable.
curriculum.security_considerations: Gemini is optional and not a paid requirement for certification. Real confidential data must never be pasted into public AI prompts.

curriculum.title: Digital Office Capstone
curriculum.objective: Integrate all primary Google Workspace applications into one complete, secure and professionally organized digital office workflow.
lessons: 6.1 Fictional Business Scenario Setup: Reviewing organizational profile, project objectives, cross-functional team roles, and milestone deliverables.
6.2 Google Drive Workspace Architecture: Creating the top-level folder hierarchy, standardizing file naming conventions, and assigning ownership.
6.3 Professional Document Production: Drafting the operational project plan in Google Docs with styles, headings, tables, and collaboration comments.
6.4 Team Operations Tracker in Sheets: Building the collaborative tracker with task IDs, owners, deadlines, data validation, and status formulas.
6.5 Executive Slides Presentation: Creating a 5- to 7-slide project briefing deck in Google Slides featuring an embedded linked chart from Sheets.
6.6 Request Intake Workflow: Designing the Google Form, linking responses to a dedicated sheet, and generating synthetic practice submissions.
6.7 Calendar & Meeting Coordination: Scheduling the team kickoff event in Calendar, setting up Meet access, and attaching the Docs agenda.
6.8 Gmail Communication Dispatch: Composing the formal project kickoff email with Drive links, explicit responsibilities, and calendar attachments.
6.9 Access Permissions Matrix Audit: Auditing Viewer, Commenter, and Editor roles across every file, folder, Form, and linked Sheet in the workspace.
6.10 Version History & Audit Trail: Documenting change logs, named revisions, and recovery readiness across Docs, Sheets, and Slides files.
6.11 Task List Integration: Organizing individual and team action items using Google Tasks integrated with Calendar deadlines.
6.12 Optional Gemini Review Application: Applying verified AI assistance to summarize the capstone report or polish communications.
6.13 Quality Assurance & Link Verification: Verifying that all internal hyperlinks, smart chips, chart connections, and permissions function flawlessly.
6.14 Safe Workspace Handover Package: Compiling the Workspace Index, folder purpose map, permission matrix, and operational handover SOP.
6.15 Final Capstone Demonstration: Presenting the complete connected office workflow, justifying access decisions, and demonstrating operational integration.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Assemble the complete fictional cloud office environment integrating all 8 applications into a cohesive operational system with audited permissions and handover documentation.
curriculum.deliverable: Collaborative Digital Office Workspace — Final Capstone
curriculum.security_considerations: Full verification of least-privilege permissions, zero public link exposure, and complete separation of synthetic practice data from personal accounts.

Identification of inherited folder permissions and segregation of restricted confidential files.
Separate verification of Google Forms collaborators vs linked response Sheet collaborators.

faq.question: What is Google Workspace — Cloud Productivity & Collaboration?
faq.answer: It is a practical course teaching connected Google applications for communication, documents, meetings, reporting and teamwork.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Five weeks with 40 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹5,900, subject to verified Nova Skills pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic computer and internet knowledge are sufficient.

faq.question: Which Google applications are covered?
faq.answer: Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Meet and Forms.

faq.question: What is the difference between a personal Google account and Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Personal accounts provide access to many Google productivity tools. Paid Workspace editions add organization-oriented controls and features depending on the plan.

faq.question: Must I purchase Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Not for every core collaboration exercise. Certain business and AI features require eligible paid plans.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Drive?
faq.answer: Yes, including folder organization, file sharing, ownership and version history.

faq.question: What are Viewer, Commenter and Editor permissions?
faq.answer: They are access roles that determine how collaborators can use or modify shared files.

faq.question: Can folder permissions affect files inside them?
faq.answer: Yes. Drive supports inherited permissions, so folder-level sharing must be reviewed.

faq.question: Will I learn Gmail productivity?
faq.answer: Yes, including professional emails, labels, filters and search.

faq.question: Will I learn Calendar scheduling?
faq.answer: Yes, including invitations, recurring meetings, meeting details and follow-ups.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Meet?
faq.answer: Yes, including meeting participation and basic coordination.

faq.question: Is Meet recording free for everyone?
faq.answer: No. Recording depends on eligible account plans and permissions.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Docs collaboration?
faq.answer: Yes, including comments, suggestions and version history.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes, for basic formulas, team trackers and reporting.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Slides?
faq.answer: Yes, for collaborative business presentations.

faq.question: Is this a complete Google Sheets or presentation design specialization?
faq.answer: No. The course focuses on practical cloud-office operations.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Forms?
faq.answer: Yes, including form creation, response collection and linking responses to Sheets.

faq.question: Do Forms and linked Sheets have the same permissions?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Their permissions may need to be reviewed separately.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Tasks?
faq.answer: Yes, as a supporting tool for basic task coordination.

faq.question: Will I learn Gemini?
faq.answer: Yes, through responsible AI assistance and eligible feature demonstrations.

faq.question: Is Gemini included in every free Google account?
faq.answer: No. Workspace-integrated Gemini capabilities depend on eligible plans and feature requirements.

faq.question: Can Gemini generate presentations in Google Slides?
faq.answer: Eligible plans support certain Gemini presentation-generation capabilities, subject to current availability and limits.

faq.question: Will I learn Apps Script?
faq.answer: Only introductory awareness or optional demonstrations. Complex scripting is excluded.

faq.question: Is a business email domain required?
faq.answer: No. The core training can use accessible tools and authorized practice accounts.

faq.question: Will I learn Workspace Admin Console?
faq.answer: No. Enterprise domain administration is outside this certification.

faq.question: What will I build for the portfolio?
faq.answer: A collaborative office workspace containing documents, a tracker, a presentation, a Forms workflow, meeting coordination and a permissions audit.

faq.question: Will the course use real company information?
faq.answer: No real confidential data is required. Synthetic or authorized practice information can be used.

faq.question: Who should enroll?
faq.answer: Office staff, remote workers, freelancers, administrators, students and entrepreneurs who need practical cloud collaboration skills.

database_and_relations_policy.heading: Connect Information Once. Use It Across the Entire Workspace.
principles: Single Source of Truth: Store data entities (Clients, Projects, Tasks) in dedicated source databases; reference them via Relations rather than duplicating text records.
Relational Integrity: Establish clean two-way relations (Client → Projects, Project → Tasks); ensure parent-child associations remain unambiguous.
Rollup Discipline: Use Rollups to summarize connected progress (task completion counts, earliest start dates) without manual spreadsheet calculations.
Source Database vs Linked View: Understand that editing a linked database view modifies the underlying source record; filters only alter visual presentation, not data storage.
View Filters Are Not Permissions: Never rely on filtered database views (e.g., 'My Assigned Tasks') to secure confidential records; anyone with source database access can view all rows.

forms_and_automations_boundary.heading: Understand What Is Manual, What Is Automated, and What Requires a Paid Plan
principles: Notion Forms Access: Basic Forms are accessible across standard Notion plans; advanced styling and conditional branching require eligible paid tiers.
Buttons vs Automations: Interactive database buttons trigger actions upon manual clicks; automated event triggers (status change, date arrival) are primarily paid features.
Automation Trigger Constraints: Free-plan automations are restricted (e.g., basic Slack alerts); multi-step triggers and cascading automations require paid plans.
Manual Fallback Requirement: All required course projects can be completed using manual updates, templates, and basic buttons—no student is forced to buy a paid plan to graduate.

notion_ai_and_agents_governance.heading: AI Can Assist Your Workspace. Human Review Must Remain in Control.
principles: Awareness of October 2026 Architecture: Covers Notion Agents, custom agent scoping, MCP connections, and the updated credit model at a practical governance level.
Credit & Plan Awareness: Educates students on monthly AI credit allocations, transition timelines (October/November 2026), and administrative spending limits.
Mandatory Human Review: Crucial changes (client statuses, task assignees, contractual terms) must be verified through Agent Review Mode before committing.
Synthetic Data Policy: No real customer lists, confidential financial records, or PII are permitted in classroom AI prompts; students use synthetic business scenarios exclusively.

knowledge_base_and_sop_standards.heading: Keep Important Knowledge Findable, Reliable, and Easy to Maintain
principles: SOP Structural Standard: Every SOP requires a clear title, business purpose, named owner, preconditions, numbered steps, expected output, quality checks, and review date.
Searchable Categorization: Knowledge assets must include logical tags, breadcrumb hierarchies, and internal links to ensure rapid retrieval during team operations.
Maintenance & Deprecation: Stale procedures degrade operational trust; workspaces must include scheduled review cycles and archived legacy documentation.
